Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule SE line 1a — net farm profit or (loss)
Fact.Description:
Schedule SE LINE 1a, printed in full as "Net farm profit or (loss) from Schedule F, line 34, and farm partnerships, Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), box 14, code A". TWO printed sources, and both are supplied, added:
Schedule F line 34 scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss, the Schedule F export, when the farm is this filer's. Taken SIGNED and UNFLOORED: a farm loss reduces line 3 and therefore reduces self-employment tax, which is what "profit or (loss)" and line 3's "Combine" both say. The floor is line 4a's, one step later, and it is applied to the COMBINED line 3, never to this term alone. farm partnership scheduleE:/primaryFilerK1FarmSeEarnings: the box 14 code A amount K-1 box 14 code A of this filer's partnership K-1s that report a farming business in box 20 code AN (scheduleE:/formK1s/*/reportsFarmingOrFishingBusiness). It is independent of who owns the Schedule F, so it is added outside that attribution. Line 2 takes the same filer's box 14 code A LESS this amount, as its printed "(other than farming)" says, so the K-1 amount reaches line 3 exactly once. Moving an amount between lines 1a and 2 does not move line 3; it moves the printed lines and what the farm optional method skips. Code AN is the partnership's "farming and fishing business" code, so a fishing partnership's box 14 code A prints here too (see the tax interpretations log).
WHOSE SCHEDULE SE THIS IS. Schedule SE is a per-individual form ("If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE"), so this term is the farm net only when the farm is the PRIMARY filer's, and $0 when it is the spouse's. The attribution comes from scheduleF:/scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler, the complement of the intake question scheduleF:/writableScheduleFBelongsToSecondaryFiler; the spouse's half of the same routing is /secondaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a. On a return that is not MFJ there is one possible farmer and the attribution's unanswered default sends the farm here; on an MFJ return that claims a farm and leaves the question blank the answer is not defaulted at all — scheduleF:/scheduleFOwnerUnansweredOnMfj blocks submission, because a silent primary default would misapply two independent per-filer fences at once (the primary's remaining $176,100 OASDI base rather than the spouse's, and the $400 line-4c threshold measured against his combined earnings rather than hers).
A QUALIFIED JOINT VENTURE (IRC 761(f)) IS SPLIT, AND IT IS THE FIRST ARM. Where both spouses materially participate in the same farm and elect to divide every Schedule F item by their respective interests, the farm is neither spouse's whole and the attribution above has nothing to say about it. This term is then scheduleF:/scheduleFQjvPrimaryFilerShare, Schedule F line 34 times the primary filer's interest, and the spouse's twin takes the remainder — the two shares partition the one line 34 by construction. The election is scheduleF:/writableScheduleFQualifiedJointVentureElection and its gate is scheduleF:/scheduleFIsQualifiedJointVenture; an elected return that never states the percentage refuses rather than defaults, because scheduleF:/writableScheduleFQjvPrimaryFilerInterestPercent carries no Placeholder and scheduleF:/scheduleFQjvInterestUnansweredOnQjv blocks submission. WHAT THE SPLIT DOES NOT REACH, because this dictionary still models ONE Schedule F rather than the two the instructions have a QJV file: the division is applied to the NET, after the section 465 at-risk cap and the section 464 prepaid-farm-supplies test have been applied to the COMBINED farm, so the figure differs from two separately-filed Schedules F exactly when one of those limits binds (direction INDETERMINATE, and nil otherwise); the line 1b Conservation Reserve Program subtraction below is NOT divided, because /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bAsCombined still routes it by scheduleF:/scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler; and nothing prints a second Schedule F.
WHAT IS NOT MODELLED, named rather than left to be found:
- LINE 1b, the Conservation Reserve Program subtraction, IS MODELLED, and not here: the amount is /writableScheduleSeLine1bConservationReservePayments, its section 1402(a)(1) benefit-timing condition is /writableScheduleSeLine1bReceivingSocialSecurityBenefits, and the reduction reaches line 3 through /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bAsCombined or its secondary twin, whichever chain owns the farm. What is still missing is only the SOURCE SPLIT: scheduleF:/scheduleFLine4b is the TOTAL taxable agricultural program payments with no CRP subset broken out, which is why the amount is asked rather than read, and a CRP amount reported in Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 20 code AQ belongs to the K-1's own filer rather than to the farm. - THE FARM OPTIONAL METHOD (Part II, lines 14 through 15). The form prints "Skip lines 1a and 1b if you use the farm optional method in Part II", so an electing filer's line 1a is not this quantity at all. Part II is not modelled and neither is the election. DIRECTION OF THE ERROR: INDETERMINATE, on the instructions' own words rather than on a guess: "This method can increase or decrease your net earnings from farm self-employment even if the farming business had a loss." Not modelling an ELECTION also means the model computes the no-election path, which is the filer's default. - FORM 4835 IS NOT A LINE 1a SOURCE, checked rather than assumed, because a Form 4835 Part I intake landed on this same trunk (dictionary/ty2025/form4835.xml) and a reader will ask. Line 1a's printed text names Schedule F line 34 and farm-partnership K-1 box 14A and nothing else; Form 4835's own printed subtitle is "(Income Not Subject to Self-Employment Tax)"; and the Schedule SE instructions say of a farm rental reported on Form 4835 that each spouse files a separate 4835 and "Don't file Schedule SE unless you have other income subject to the SE tax." Form 4835's net reaches this return through Schedule E, not through this line. No wiring is owed.
A PRE-EXISTING LINE-4a DIVERGENCE, DISCLOSED HERE — AND ITS "OVER-TAXES" CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN AS FALSE (tested). The divergence itself is real: printed line 4a reads "If line 3 is more than zero, multiply line 3 by 92.35% (0.9235). Otherwise, enter amount from line 3", so a NEGATIVE line 3 is carried to line 4a unchanged, while /primaryFilerNetEarningsFromSelfEmployment floors at $0. A farm loss is now a second way to drive line 3 negative; a Schedule C loss was the first. WHAT WAS WRONG was the consequence: this text claimed the two readings "diverge on line 6, where a filer with church employee income adds line 5b to line 4c", and that the module therefore OVER-taxes that filer. It does not. Line 4c is "Combine lines 4a and 4b", and line 4b (the Part II optional methods) is unmodeled and always 0 here — so a negative line 4a is ALWAYS below $400, and printed line 4c's own instruction then replaces it with zero before line 5b is ever added: "stop" when there is no church employee income, "enter -0- and continue" when there is. The printed form zeroes the negative itself. The module's line 6 (/primaryFilerTotalNetEarningsSubjectToSeTax) implements exactly that floor-then-add Switch, so both readings enter 0 on line 4c and reach the SAME line 6. The floor is UNOBSERVABLE from line 4c down, not adverse. WITNESSED, not merely argued, by node test scheduleSE/se4a-negative-line3-church-income-floor-unobservable: line 3 = -20,100 with $20,000 of church employee income yields line 6 = 18,470.00, which is line 5b exactly — the negative contributes nothing under either reading. THE CONDITION THAT WOULD MAKE IT REACHABLE, for whoever trips it: line 4b. If the Part II optional methods (lines 15 and 17) are ever built, a positive 4b could lift line 4c to $400 or more WHILE line 4a is negative, and only then would the printed negative reduce line 6 where the floored zero does not. Whoever models the optional methods must remove this floor in the same unit, and must re-point the witness above. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Schedule SE line 1a — net farm profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Schedule SE LINE 1a on the SECONDARY (MFJ spouse) filer's own Schedule SE: scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss when the farm this return reports is hers, and $0 otherwise. The twin of /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a, and the same single Schedule F line 34 read through the opposite arm of the same attribution — the two Schedule F terms are mutually exclusive and never both nonzero, because this dictionary models one farm. Taken SIGNED and UNFLOORED, exactly as the primary twin is: a farm loss reduces HER line 3 and therefore her self-employment tax. The $400 floor is line 4a's, one step later, and it applies to her COMBINED line 3, never to this term alone — which is the whole point of attributing at all, since a farm measured against her own $176,100 OASDI base and her own $400 threshold is a different tax than the same farm measured against his. Complete-safe $0 on every return that is not MFJ and on every joint return whose farm is the primary filer's, so it is additive for the existing corpus. THE QUALIFIED JOINT VENTURE ARM COMES FIRST, and on that arm the two terms are BOTH nonzero rather than mutually exclusive: an elected QJV farm (IRC 761(f)) is divided between the spouses by their respective interests, so this term is scheduleF:/scheduleFQjvSecondaryFilerShare, which is Schedule F line 34 minus the primary filer's share. The pair still partitions the one line 34 exactly; what changes is that the partition can be uneven rather than all-or-nothing. The reasoning, the refusal on a blank interest percentage and the residue are stated once, on the primary twin. The farm-partnership Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A half of the printed line is scheduleE:/secondaryFilerK1FarmSeEarnings, her own K-1s that report box 20 code AN, added outside the Schedule F attribution and left out of her line 2, as on the primary twin.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's net profit or (loss) from self-employment (Schedule SE line 3)
Fact.Description: The PRIMARY filer's Schedule SE line 3, "Combine lines 1a, 1b, and 2": his LINE 1a net farm profit or loss (/primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a) PLUS the LINE 2 Schedule C net profit ATTRIBUTED to him (scheduleC:/primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit) PLUS the box-14A partnership SE earnings attributed to him (scheduleE:/primaryFilerK1SeEarnings), LESS his LINE 1b Conservation Reserve Program payments (/primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bAsCombined, already negated) and LESS his notary-public net profit (/primaryFilerScheduleSeNotaryNetProfitAsCombined, already negated, the i1040sse line-3 dotted-line adjustment for IRC 1402(c)(1) fee-basis public office income), LESS his ministerial net earnings excluded under an approved Form 4361 (/primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined, already negated, IRC 1402(e)), PLUS his section 1402(a)(8) minister add-back, the parsonage or housing allowance and the section 119 meals and lodging that line 2 includes (/primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack, $0 unless he is a minister without an approved Form 4361), and LESS his section 1402(a)(3) trader carve-out (/primaryFilerScheduleSeTraderScheduleCExclusionAsCombined, already negated), and PLUS OR LESS his community-income dotted-line adjustments (/primaryFilerScheduleSeCommunityIncomeAdjustmentAsCombined, already combined signed), and PLUS his ministerial-service W-2 wages attributed to him (/primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterW2SalaryIncluded), counted once beyond their unchanged Form 1040 line 1a treatment, and his LINE 2 wages as a U.S. citizen employed by a foreign government or an international organization for services performed in the United States or a listed possession (/primaryFilerScheduleSeForeignGovernmentEmployeeIncomeIncluded) - an inclusion section 1402(c)(2)(C) makes, not a relief. The eleven terms combine SIGNED and BEFORE the line-4a floor, so a farm LOSS reduces his Schedule C and partnership earnings on this one line, exactly as a Schedule C loss already reduced his partnership earnings ("if you had a loss in one business, it reduces the income from another"). Signed: a combined loss stays negative here and is floored at zero one step later, on line 4a/4c. Deliberately does NOT read the SECONDARY filer's Schedule C or K-1 earnings — "no part of your share can be included in figuring your spouse's net earnings from self-employment" (2025 Instructions for Schedule SE, Community income). interpretation:provisional — CHOSEN READING: line 3 is computed PER SCHEDULE SE, so this chain sums only the terms attributed to THIS filer and a loss here never reaches the spouse's line 3. REJECTED: a single combined line 3 that nets both spouses' businesses before the line-4a floor, which is what the single-chain model computed and which the Community-income sentence forbids. The two readings diverge on exactly one shape — a LOSS on one spouse's chain against a PROFIT on the other's — and a node test of a joint return with a Schedule C loss on one spouse and a K-1 profit on the other is drawn to be that shape and pins it. THE SCHEDULE C FILER ATTRIBUTION CLOSED THE SECOND READING THIS FACT USED TO CARRY. It formerly read the whole /scheduleCNetProfit on the standing simplification that the modeled Schedule C is the primary's, and disclosed the residual: an MFJ return whose SPOUSE owned both a Schedule C and a K-1 split that one person's self-employment income across two Schedules SE, which section 1402 requires be computed on one. scheduleC:/scheduleCFiler now attributes the business, so that residual is gone and no interpretation is needed here for it; the attribution's own provisional reading (unanswered proprietor defaults to the primary filer) lives on /scheduleCFiler, where it is made.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule SE line 8a — W-2 boxes 3 and 7 plus railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation
Fact.Description:
Schedule SE LINE 8a on the PRIMARY filer's own Schedule SE, printed in full as "Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2) and railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation". THREE ADDENDS, summed over that filer's OWN W-2s (formW2s:/primaryFilerW2s), because the wage base is a per-person limit and each spouse files a separate Schedule SE: box 3 (formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWagesUnrounded), box 7 (formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiTipsUnrounded) and box 14 railroad retirement compensation (formW2s:/formW2s/*/rrtaCompensationUnrounded).
THE TWO TERMS BESIDE BOX 3 cut in one direction: leaving either out makes 8a low, so line 9 (the remaining base) high, so line 10's smaller-of lets more self-employment earnings through at 12.4% and OVERSTATES SE tax (taxpayer-adverse). The box-7 arm is witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleSE/se8a-box7-tips-same-total-different-split, which holds the same 174,000 of compensation as the shipping se8-line8d-8919-wages-shrink-base-headroom but splits it 170,000 box 3 / 4,000 box 7: SE tax 816 either way (box 3 alone would give the split return 1,312). The RRTA arm is witnessed by se8a-rrta-compensation-consumes-base, a railroad W-2 carrying the same 174,000 in box 14 with boxes 3 through 7 empty: 816 (box 3 alone would give 4,239, handing a railroad filer back a base they had already spent).
NO CAP, AND THAT IS RE-DERIVED FROM THE PRINTED LINE RATHER THAN INHERITED. The old shape summed LesserOf(Round(box 3), $176,100) per W-2. That per-item ceiling is not printed on 8a; it comes from formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWagesForKnockoutCalculation, whose own Description states a different purpose — it exists so the multi-W-2 OASDI KNOCKOUT does not fire on filers whose W-2s do not all carry social security wages. Printed 8a is a plain total of box figures, and the wage base enters this schedule exactly ONCE, at line 9's "Subtract line 8d from line 7. If zero or less, enter -0-". The near-verbatim printed twin already adjudicated in this repo agrees on the no-cap reading for the WAGES-AND-TIPS terms: form4137:/primaryFilerForm4137Line8 is Form 4137 line 8, "Total social security wages and social security tips (total of your Form(s) W-2, boxes 3 and 7)" — it also carries the RRTA term, which Form 4137's OWN printed instruction caps at the wage base while Schedule SE prints no counterpart cap; the wages/tips terms stay uncapped on both.
THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, PRICED RATHER THAN DISMISSED: keep a per-item ceiling and move it onto the combined per-employer figure, LesserOf(box 3 + box 7 + box 14, $176,100). It has a landed sibling in schedule3:/formW2s/*/oasdiAndTier1WagesForExcessEligibility, and it is rejected on two counts. First, that sibling caps because Schedule 3 line 11's test IS a $176,100 gate, so the ceiling serves the gate's own semantics; 8a is a subtrahend, not a gate. Second, the ceiling is unobservable past this fact: whenever it could bite, that one item is already at or above the base, so line 8d is too, so line 9 floors to zero either way — and that is now MEASURED over the whole 942-case materialized corpus rather than argued, by a before/after differential across every resolved row. Six paths change in total, and /…SeRemainingSocialSecurityBase (line 9) changes on exactly TWO cases, the two where the box-7 and railroad terms actually land. Line 8d's own value and its alias move on 119; on the 117 that are not those two, they move and NOTHING ELSE does, with line 9 unmoved at 0.00 and no tax row anywhere in the corpus moving. ONE CONSUMER OUTSIDE THIS SCHEDULE reads 8d and is named here so the census is complete (loop-8 fg-review): form2210's Schedule AI Part II attestation fence (form2210:/form2210ScheduleAiPart2AttestationsConsistentPrimary) equality-checks line 30 col (d) against this fact and REFUSES on mismatch — no committed scenario answers those attestations today, and the fence's failure mode is refusal, never a wrong dollar; but the first Schedule AI scenario authored against pre-loop-8 8d values will trip it and must use the rebuilt figures. Those 117 are all box-3 figures above the statutory per-employer ceiling of 176,100, which no correctly issued W-2 can carry (layerA holds 190,000, 269,210, 279,190 and 310,000; layerB's taxable-income sweep runs up to 783,101). THE STRONGEST LINE IS NOT THE ROW COUNT BUT THE INCONSISTENCY IT REMOVES: this repo already shipped a second fact computing boxes 3 and 7 over the same formW2s:/primaryFilerW2s, and it is uncapped, so the two DISAGREED. On one captured head-of-household case, aged 65 or over, the captured rows read form4137:/primaryFilerForm4137Line8 = 220,924.00 against this chain's 176,100.00 — 44,824 apart on one filer's one W-2. Carrying the ceiling here would have kept that contradiction and put it on a third fact. A ceiling whose only observable effect is truncating out-of-range data is a data-hygiene guard, and 8a does not print one. The boundary case tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleSE/se8a-over-base-rrta-uncapped-line9-zero pins both halves: 8a carried whole at 200,000, and line 9 at 0.00 with the capped counterfactual's own zero beside it in the transcript.
ONE ROUND, AT THE PRINTED LINE, over cents-bearing addends. 8a adds two or more amounts, so i1040gi page 23 governs — "include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total" — and the three Unrounded twins are exactly the addend facts that rule needs. Summing the per-W-2 rounded entry facts instead is the sum-of-rounded-addends defect verbatim (two W-2s at 100.40 each total 200.80, so the line is 201, while the sum of rounded items is 200), and the old shape had it: it summed formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWages, which is Round(...). This is the same remedy already applied to box 5, to box 4 and to box 1.
WHY THIS IS NOT BUILT ON form4137:/primaryFilerForm4137Line8, which is the reuse a reader will reach for first, since that fact is exactly this one's first two addends. It is Round-wrapped, and Round(Round(A) + B) is not Round(A + B) — reusing it would re-introduce a sum-of-rounded-addends seam of up to a dollar for any railroad filer whose box-3-plus-7 and box-14 figures both carry cents, which is the very defect class the paragraph above removes. No unrounded per-filer sibling exists in form4137 to build on. [FORWARD POINTER CLOSED: the RRTA term landed on Form 4137 line 8 — but CAPPED at the wage base, as that form's own printed instruction requires and Schedule SE's does not, so the two facts CANNOT be expressed through each other on substance, not rounding. The non-reuse decision above stands, strengthened.]
NOT form8959:/rrtaCompensationAndTips either, although it is the module's existing box-14 total. That fact is a deliberate JOINT aggregate — Form 8959 line 15 applies one threshold to the couple — while Schedule SE is per filer, "each must file a separate Schedule SE". Reading it here would charge a spouse's railroad compensation against this filer's base.
THE DISCLOSED RESIDUAL, with its direction, because it points the OTHER way from the two gaps this fact closes and a reader is owed that. Box 14 reports TOTAL RRTA compensation, which is Medicare-equivalent and uncapped, while printed 8a wants the tier-1 compensation subject to the 6.2% rate. The two coincide for an ordinary railroad employee and diverge for one with pay that is Medicare-taxable but tier-1-exempt, whose box-14 figure then exceeds their tier-1 base — so 8a reads HIGH, line 9 reads LOW, and SE tax is at or below correct. schedule3:/formW2s/*/oasdiAndTier1WagesForExcessEligibility records the same residual with its own bound. It is a property of reading box 14 at all, not of this fact's shape, and no W-2 field reports the tier-1 wage base separately, so closing it needs an intake that does not exist.
COMPLETENESS IS UNCHANGED FROM THE SHAPE THIS REPLACES, and it is witnessed rather than argued. All three addend facts carry the module's IsComplete/Switch wrapper resolving an unanswered box to $0, so an unanswered intake never makes this Incomplete, and a return with no W-2 gives 8a = $0 rather than Incomplete. Where /formW2s is itself a Placeholder this fact is Placeholder too, exactly as the old dependency was, and that is READ OFF THE RESOLVED TREE rather than inferred from a sibling's behaviour. The Round wrapper introduced here therefore cannot delete a captured row by turning Placeholder into Incomplete — the same differential that measured the value moves reports 1,884 added rows and ZERO removed.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's social security base already used, wages plus Forms 4137 and 8919 (Schedule SE line 8d)
Fact.Description:
Schedule SE LINE 8d on the PRIMARY filer's own Schedule SE, "Add lines 8a, 8b, and 8c": everything that has already used part of that filer's line-7 base before their self-employment earnings reach line 9. The path name says 8a because 8a was once the whole of this fact; the quantity is now the full line 8d, and renaming the path would remove 900-odd baseline rows for a spelling.
LINE 8a is /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine8a, and IT IS NOW THE WHOLE OF THE PRINTED LINE: W-2 boxes 3 and 7 plus box-14 railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation, summed over that filer's own W-2s under a single Round. Read that fact for the no-cap re-derivation, the single-Round rule and the box-14 residual. WHAT THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY, recorded because this fact's own history is the argument for the fix: the term used to be formW2s:/primaryFilerTotalOasdiWagesForKnockout, box 3 alone and per-item capped at the wage base, so a filer with box-7 tips or with railroad compensation had line 8a understated, line 9 overstated and SE tax OVERSTATED — taxpayer-ADVERSE, twice over on the same printed line. Both omissions were disclosed here as latent, and both were: the box-7 case scenarios/upstream/hoh-20k.json and the railroad case scenarios/units/rrr each resolve /selfEmploymentTax 0.00, so closing the gaps moved their captured 8a and line-9 rows without moving any tax. That latency is why the two arms needed authored witnesses rather than a corpus case to prove them, and they have three; see the fact.
LINE 8b is form4137:/primaryFilerForm4137Line10, unreported tips subject to social security tax, and LINE 8c is form8919:/primaryFilerForm8919Line10, wages subject to social security tax from a firm that withheld none. Both facts carry their own tax-side consumers; the residue was a line 8 short by both terms, so line 9 was HIGH, so line 10 read min(line 6, an inflated line 9) and SE tax was OVERSTATED for any filer whose self-employment earnings plus Form 4137 tips plus Form 8919 wages exceed the $176,100 base. Taxpayer-ADVERSE, and closed here. Measured on tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleSE/se8-line8d-tips-and-8919-wages-lower-se-tax: 1,560 of SE tax before, 816 after, on a return with 4,000 of unreported tips and 2,000 of Form 8919 wages.
NO "SKIP LINES 8b THROUGH 10" BRANCH IS MODELLED, and none is owed. Line 8a's printed instruction ("If $176,100 or more, skip lines 8b through 10, and go to line 11") names an OUTCOME this arithmetic already produces: with 8a at or above the base, line 9's own printed zero floor makes line 10 zero and only the uncapped line 11 survives, which is what "go to line 11" means; and both cross-form line 10s are themselves smaller-of comparisons against their own zeroed line 9, so 8b and 8c self-zero in that state as well. The boundary pair tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleSE/se8-line8d-8919-wages-at-wage-base-no-effect against se8-line8d-8919-wages-shrink-base-headroom holds the same 2,000 of Form 8919 wages against 8a = 176,100 and 8a = 174,000: SE tax 803 either way on the first, 1,064 against 816 on the second.
NO ROUND, and that is a checked identity rather than an inherited shape. All three addends are whole dollars by construction: 8a is /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine8a, which is itself a Round at its own printed line (it was once a CollectionSum of LesserOf(Round(box 3), $176,100), whole-dollar for a different reason — the enumeration changed with that fill and the conclusion did not); Form 4137 line 10 is a smaller-of whose minuend subtracts the government-employee carve-out (itself LesserOf(Round(...), line 6), so whole-dollar) from a line 6 built from Rounded lines 2, 3 and 5, against a line 9 built from a Rounded line 8; Form 8919 line 10 is the plain smaller-of with NO carve-out, as its own body states. A Round here would be a value-identity no-op and a divergence from this fact's own no-Round history.
COMPLETENESS IS UNCHANGED, AND IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED, because a reshape that moves completeness moves committed rows even at an unmoved value. Fact.Name: Church employee income from Form W-2 (Schedule SE line 5a)

Fact.Name: Primary filer's church employee income, 92.35% adjusted (Schedule SE line 5b)
Fact.Description: Schedule SE line 5b: /writableChurchEmployeeIncome x 92.35%, floored to $0 when the result is under $100 ("Multiply line 5a by 92.35% (0.9235). If less than $100, enter -0-") — the SAME 92.35% employer-equivalent haircut line 4a applies, with its own separate $100 (not $400) floor. THE $100 COMPARISON IS UNROUNDED, a deliberate choice disclosed because the alternative is close enough to bite: the $100 test here compares the RAW (unrounded, full-precision) 92.35% product against $100, not a whole-dollar-rounded intermediate. The Instructions for Schedule SE state a practical equivalent: "If you had church employee income of $108.28 or more, you must pay SE tax" (i1040sse). That published figure is NOT the exact algebraic breakeven of this unrounded test. ⚠ THE ARITHMETIC IN THIS PARAGRAPH WAS ONCE WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY SWAPPED, because an interpretation:provisional tag rests on it. It read "100 / 0.9235 = 108.2619..., i.e. $108.27 already clears the raw product past $100" and called the divergence "a roughly two-cent input band ($108.27-$108.28)". Both figures are false. The true breakeven is 100 / 0.9235 = 108.283703...; at $108.27 the raw product is 0.9235 x 108.27 = $99.987345, which does NOT clear $100; the FIRST cent that clears is $108.29 (0.9235 x 108.29 = $100.005815). At exactly $108.28 the raw product is $99.99658 — UNDER $100 on this fact's unrounded test, so it floors to $0, which is the divergence from i1040sse's own stated figure and is real. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: round the 92.35% product to the nearest whole dollar BEFORE comparing it to $100. Under that reading the test clears once the raw product reaches $99.50, i.e. from an input of $107.75 (0.9235 x 107.75 = $99.507125, HALF_UP to $100) — $107.74 gives $99.49789 and still fails. So the TRUE DIVERGENCE BAND is $107.75 through $108.28 inclusive: 54 distinct cents of input, not two. The prior "two-cent" claim understated it roughly 27-fold, and that is the correction that matters — the band is narrow but it is not a rounding curiosity. THE CONSEQUENCE INSIDE THE BAND is unchanged and is real, not academic: a filer there gets $0 here (this fact's chosen reading) versus a floored $100 flowing to line 6 (the rejected reading) — $100 x 15.3% (12.4% + 2.9%) = $15.30 of self-employment tax, in the UNDER-COLLECTION direction, so this fact's chosen reading is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE across the whole band. THE SHIPPED <Derived> BELOW IS NOT CHANGED by this correction and is the statutorily defensible reading: IRC 1402(j)(2)(B) substitutes "$100" for "$400" in subsection (b)(2), which tests the net earnings figure itself, not a rounded rendering of it. Only the disclosure's arithmetic was wrong.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's total net earnings subject to SE tax (Schedule SE line 6)
Fact.Description: Schedule SE line 6: "Add lines 4c and 5b." Line 4c itself is /primaryFilerNetEarningsFromSelfEmployment (line 4a, since the unmodeled optional-method line 4b is always 0) WHEN that figure is $400 or more; below $400 the line-4c instruction floors the entry to $0 REGARDLESS of church employee income ("stop" when there is none, "enter -0-" when there is) before line 5b is added — so a sub-$400 filer's line 6 is driven entirely by church employee income, never by the below-floor line-4c figure itself. Feeds the line 10 (social security) and line 11 (medicare) computations, replacing line 4c/4a as their base now that a nonzero line 5b exists. THE STATUTORY BASIS for floor-then-add (why the $400 test binds line 4c ALONE, separately from the $100 test on line 5b, rather than a combined figure being tested once): IRC §1402(j)(2)(A) requires "Paragraph (2) of subsection (b) [the $400/$100 threshold rule] shall be applied SEPARATELY — (i) to church employee income, and (ii) to other net earnings from self-employment." The two floors are legally independent tests on two different bases, which is exactly the floor-then-add shape below (each Switch branch applies its own threshold before the Add combines the results) and is exactly what a naive combined-then-floor implementation would violate.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's net profit or (loss) from self-employment (Schedule SE line 3)
Fact.Description:

HER LINE 2 ALSO CARRIES her own ministerial-service W-2 wages (/secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterW2SalaryIncluded) and her foreign-government or international-organization wages (/secondaryFilerScheduleSeForeignGovernmentEmployeeIncomeIncluded) and her own section 1402(a)(8) minister add-back (/secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack), on her own Schedule SE and measured against her own wage base and her own $400 threshold. HER LINE 1a IS THE THIRD TERM: /secondaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a, the Schedule F line 34 net when the farm this return reports is HERS rather than his. REJECTED: floor each source separately (max(0, Schedule C) + max(0, K-1)), which would tax her partnership earnings ungrossed by her own business loss. Fact.Name: Net earnings from self-employment (combined Schedule SE Part I line 6, Form 8959 line 8)
Fact.Description:
The return-level total of Schedule SE PART I LINE 6 across BOTH filers' Schedules SE — the figure Form 8959 line 8 names verbatim, and the only consumer this fact has. Line 3's two named sources are Schedule C net profit and Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A; the per-filer split of those sources happens one level down, in /primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss and /secondaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss. NOTE this is a SUM of two independently-computed line 6s, not a line 6 of a combined line 3: one spouse's SE loss does not offset the other's profit ("no part of your share can be included in figuring your spouse's net earnings from self-employment"), and each filer's $400 line-4c floor and $100 line-5b floor are applied on that filer's OWN Schedule SE before the two totals meet here (IRC 1402(j)(2)(A)). interpretation:provisional.
REBODIED (the Form 8959 line-8 successor), CLOSING TWO MEASURED DIVERGENCES this fact's Description previously only disclosed. Until this rebody the body was Add(/primaryFilerNetEarningsFromSelfEmployment, /secondaryFilerNetEarningsFromSelfEmployment) — the two RAW line 4a figures — which (1) did NOT apply the $400 line-4c floor, an OVER-COLLECTION of Additional Medicare Tax (taxpayer-ADVERSE), and (2) did NOT add either filer's line 5b church employee income, an UNDER-COLLECTION (taxpayer-FAVOURABLE). Both are now fixed by reading the two per-filer line-6 facts, which already floor-then-add correctly. WHAT MOVED, so the change is auditable rather than asserted: three committed scenarios (369 -> 0, 399 -> 0 and 277 -> 0) and six node-tests, of which the load-bearing pair are tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleSE/church-secondary-only-value-example (396 -> 18,470, BOTH divergences firing on one return) and the fresh witness tests/nodes/ty2025/form8959/f8959-line8-church-income-crosses-threshold, where line 4a of 195,000 sits below the 200,000 single-filer threshold but line 6 of 241,175 does not: Form 8959 line 13 moves 0 -> 371. Nothing downstream of a sub-$400 correction moved, because on every such return Form 8959 line 11 still holds the whole unspent threshold.
THE COMPLETENESS DESIGN, which is the hard half of this fill and the reason it was a contract rather than a two-line swap. The obvious rebody — just swapping the Add's two dependencies for the two line-6 facts — WAS TRIED, AND REGRESSES, and the regression is a COMPLETENESS one that no value-diff can catch. MEASURED, on a node test of a return REFUSED for a negative K-1 box 14A: /netEarningsFromSelfEmployment goes Incomplete -> Placeholder 0.00, and — worse, and not recorded by the contract that named this trap — /totalTax goes Incomplete -> Placeholder too, so a refused return would resolve a bottom-line total tax it must not have. WHY: /{primary,secondary}FilerTotalNetEarningsSubjectToSeTax open with a Switch on GreaterThanOrEqual(line 4a, 400); when line 4a is Incomplete that condition is Incomplete, the Switch falls through with its accumulated completeness already false, and the engine returns the fall-through arm AS A PLACEHOLDER (Expression.switches.resultRecurse). Add then propagates Incomplete only if an addend is Incomplete — a Placeholder addend yields a Placeholder — so the refusal's Incomplete was being swallowed one level down. THE FIX is the Switch below, and its guard is a completeness guard, not a tax rule: All(IsComplete(primary line 4a), IsComplete(secondary line 4a)). IsComplete always returns a COMPLETE boolean (IsCompleteOperator returns Result(x.complete, true)) and All short-circuits to Complete(false), so this Switch can never manufacture a Placeholder of its own. When the guard holds, both line-6 facts are provably Complete too (each is Add(Switch(complete condition), line 5b), and line 5b is complete-safe by its own IsComplete-first wrapper), so the true-line-6 arm renders Complete. When the guard fails, the fall-through arm is the PRE-REBODY body itself, whose rendering in that state is therefore byte-identical to what shipped: Incomplete when a line-4a fact is Incomplete, and the same Placeholder of the same raw sum when one is a Placeholder. That arm can never render a Complete value — the guard is false exactly when one of its two addends is not Complete. WHY NOT FIX THE PER-FILER FACTS INSTEAD: their Placeholder rendering is itself pinned (the same node test asserts /primaryFilerTotalNetEarningsSubjectToSeTax Placeholder 0.00 and /selfEmploymentTax Placeholder 0.00 on that same refused return), so making them Incomplete would move a wider surface for no gain here. The narrow guard keeps the blast radius at this one fact.

(writable) Form 7206 line 1: the total paid in 2025 for health insurance coverage established under the business, for the filer, spouse, dependents, AND any child of the filer (as defined in IRC section 152(f)(1)) who had not attained age 27 by the end of 2025, whether or not that child is the filer's dependent — a fourth coverage head, IRC section 162(l)(1)(D). Medicare premiums voluntarily paid for insurance similar to qualifying private coverage COUNT toward this total. Fact.Name: Self-employment tax
Fact.Description: The return's total self-employment tax: Schedule SE line 12 from the primary filer's Schedule SE plus line 12 from the secondary filer's, each zero when that filer's own net earnings are under $400. Flows to Schedule 2 line 4 / line 21 and into total tax (Form 1040 line 23).

Fact.Name: Total self-employment income including excluded territory income (Pub. 570 denominator)
Fact.Description:
The DENOMINATOR of Publication 570 chapter 4's self-employment fraction: "Total self-employment income (including excluded territory income)". Built as the two filers' Schedule SE line 3s added — /primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss plus /secondaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss — because line 3 is exactly that quantity already.
WHY LINE 3 NEEDS NO ADD-BACK, which is the one thing a reader is likely to try to "fix". Section 1402(a)(6) computes net earnings from self-employment "without regard to section 933", so the excluded territory income never left line 3 in the first place. This dictionary's Schedule SE chains read scheduleC:/primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit and /secondaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit — the COMBINED line 31, not scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax — which the possession-income review measured and this unit preserves. Adding the exclusion back here would double-count it.
A SUM OF TWO LINE 3s, NOT A COMBINED LINE 3, and the distinction is the per-filer split's: each spouse files their own Schedule SE and the two never net. It is deliberately taken BEFORE the 92.35% haircut and BEFORE the $400 and wage-base fences, because the publication's fraction is over self-employment INCOME rather than over taxable net earnings, and because a fraction taken after a per-filer floor would not be a fraction of anything the sentence names.
SIGNED. A return whose businesses net to a LOSS has a non-positive denominator; every consumer guards on /hasSelfEmploymentExclusionProration, which requires it to be strictly positive, so no divide ever sees a zero or negative divisor. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Self-employment income subject to U.S. income tax (Pub. 570 numerator)
Fact.Description:
The NUMERATOR of Publication 570 chapter 4's self-employment fraction: "Self-employment income subject to U.S. income tax" = /selfEmploymentIncomeIncludingExcludedTerritory less the excluded Schedule C net profit (scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit), FLOORED AT $0, plus /primaryFilerScheduleSeTraderExcludedTerritoryAddBack: a section 1402(a)(3) trader's Schedule C profit is not self-employment income at all, so its excluded share is outside the denominator already and must not leave the numerator a second time.
THE FLOOR IS A CLAMP WITH A DIRECTION, not tidying. The subtrahend is capped per business at that business's own line 31, but the denominator is a RETURN-level combination in which a loss business can offset a profitable one — so an excluding filer whose other business ran a large loss produces a NEGATIVE raw numerator. scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax's own Description works the shape: a 60,000 fully excluded business beside a 55,000 loss. Unfloored, the fraction goes NEGATIVE, /selfEmploymentTaxOnNonexcludedIncome goes negative, and Schedule 1 line 15 becomes an ADDITION to adjusted gross income — an arithmetic impossibility, not a small error. DIRECTION of the floor: the deduction goes to $0, which is taxpayer-ADVERSE against the unfloored arithmetic and is ALSO the answer Publication 1321 states flatly for the all-excluded case ("you cannot deduct one-half of self-employment tax (Schedule SE) if you are excluding your self-employment income (Schedule C)").
THE FRACTION CANNOT EXCEED ONE, and that needs no second clamp: the subtrahend is non-negative, so the numerator never exceeds the denominator.
⚠ ONLY SCHEDULE C EXCLUSIONS REACH THIS FACT. The graph's one possession-source income intake is the per-Schedule-C one the possession-income intake work built. A filer whose excluded territory self-employment income arrived through a Schedule K-1 box 14 code A or a Schedule F has no place to say so, so the numerator is too HIGH, the fraction too large and the deduction too LARGE — taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. That is the same intake gap scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit discloses for the oil-and-gas working interest, widened by one fraction; it is detected, not fixed, by scheduleC:/possessionUntreatedScheduleCNetProfit only when a Schedule C is also present. ⚠ IT IS NOW DETECTED IN ITS OWN RIGHT: /possessionUntreatedNonScheduleCSelfEmployment below is condition (vi) of ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion and fires on a profitable K-1 box 14 code A or Schedule F amount whether or not a Schedule C is present. STILL NOT FIXED — the intake does not exist and a refusal is not an intake — and the same gap now runs through Schedule 8812 line 18a as well, because /selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax reads both addends whole. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Self-employment income the possession intake cannot reach — a K-1 box 14 code A, a Schedule F, or an oil-and-gas working interest
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the return carries self-employment earnings from a Schedule K-1 box 14 code A, a Schedule F, or an oil-and-gas working interest routed to Schedule C line 31 (scheduleE:/workingInterestNetProfit). A KNOCKOUT INPUT AND NOTHING ELSE: it is condition (vi) of ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion. It changes no deduction, no credit and no income.
THIRD ARM, THE WORKING INTEREST, distinct from the K-1/Schedule-F arm. The working interest joins Schedule C line 31 from OUTSIDE the /scheduleCs collection (see scheduleE:/workingInterestNetProfit's own Description), so the CollectionSums over /scheduleCs/* that scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit and scheduleC:/possessionUntreatedScheduleCNetProfit read cannot see it. Without this arm a bona fide Puerto Rico resident with a territory-sourced working interest would be neither refused nor excluded from the Publication 570 fraction's numerator or Schedule 8812 line 18a, both too HIGH (taxpayer-FAVOURABLE). Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleSE/se-possession-working-interest-detected. The sibling scheduleC.xml facts do not yet carry the same widening for the exclusion FRACTION itself (the other residue).
THE WORKING-INTEREST ARM NOW ASKS FIRST, AND DISCHARGES BY ANSWERING. scheduleC:/writableWorkingInterestExcludedTerritoryNetProfit asks how much of the working interest profit is excluded possession income. Answered $0 (a well whose income is not from sources within the possession, which IRC 933(1) and 931(a) never exclude), there is nothing untreated and this arm is off: tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleSE/pr933-working-interest-us-well-no-excluded-part-files resolves this fact and ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion false. Unanswered, or answered above $0 (the excluded part is not yet apportioned), it fires as before. The scope-refusal paragraphs below (no question to answer, permanent over-refusal) now describe the K-1 and Schedule F arms only.
WHAT IT DETECTS, and it is the intake gap /selfEmploymentIncomeSubjectToUsTax has disclosed since the possession apportionment. The graph's ONE possession-source income intake is the per-Schedule-C one the possession-income intake work built (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/writableExcludedTerritoryNetProfit). A filer whose excluded territory self-employment income arrived through a K-1, a Schedule F, or an unattributable working interest HAS NO PLACE TO SAY SO, and the amount then sits, untreated, in two places at once: • the Publication 570 chapter 4 fraction's numerator (/selfEmploymentIncomeSubjectToUsTax) — too HIGH, so the fraction is too large and the half-SE-tax deduction too LARGE; • Schedule 8812 line 18a (/selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax, which reads both addends WHOLE) — too HIGH, so the additional child tax credit is too LARGE. BOTH TAXPAYER-FAVOURABLE. Before this fact NOTHING DETECTED EITHER: condition (v) fires on an unasked SCHEDULE C, so it caught this population only when a Schedule C happened to be present as well.
IT IS A SCOPE REFUSAL, NOT A DATA-COMPLETENESS ONE, and the distinction is worth keeping. Conditions (i), (iii), (iv) and (v) all discharge by ANSWERING A QUESTION — an answered $0 is enough. This one cannot: there is no question to answer, because the intake does not exist. It discharges when someone BUILDS it. That is condition (ii)'s class (scheduleA:/possessionUnapportionedCharitableCarryover), and it is named here so the successor knows which kind of work retires it.
DELIBERATELY NOT CONDITIONED ON THE EXCLUSION. The knockout's outer conjunct already requires a non-zero Schedule 8812 line 2a or 2c, so this is a bare "is there such income" question and is TRUE on plenty of ordinary returns the knockout never looks at — the same posture scheduleC:/possessionUntreatedScheduleCNetProfit takes.
PROFIT ONLY, matching condition (v)'s "PROFITABLE Schedule C" shape. A farm LOSS or a negative K-1 leg left untreated moves the two consumers in OPPOSITE directions (a smaller line 18a, a larger fraction), so the residual is unsigned and refusing on it would be refusing without a direction. Stated rather than left implicit.
THE IsComplete GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING. scheduleE:/k1SeEarnings is INCOMPLETE on a return with a negative K-1 SE amount whose DEDUCTIBLE part the partner has not stated, and a bare GreaterThan on it would propagate Incomplete into the knockout and from there into flow:/flowIsKnockedOut. The fall-through arm is TRUE — "we cannot tell, so refuse" — which is the conservative direction and costs nothing on that population, because such a return is already refused by scheduleE:/knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings and, absent an exclusion entry, the knockout's outer All short-circuits before reaching this member.
NARROWED UNDERNEATH THIS FACT, stated because the sentence above used to be true of EVERY negative K-1 SE amount and is now true only of part of them: a declared negative box 14A with a stated, internally consistent scheduleE:/formK1s/*/writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss now makes scheduleE:/k1SeEarnings COMPLETE and NEGATIVE. Such a return reaches this member with a resolvable value, the GreaterThan resolves FALSE, and this member is false rather than the fall-through TRUE. That is the correct direction (a negative K-1 SE total is not "self-employment income exists" for the purpose this member tests) and it is a strictly smaller refusal, but it is a real behavioural consequence of the box-14A fill rather than a no-op.
⚠ IT OVER-REFUSES, AND THE OVER-REFUSAL IS PERMANENT RATHER THAN DISCHARGEABLE. It asks whether such income EXISTS, not whether any of it is territory-sourced — because nothing collects the second question, which is the whole gap. So it refuses a bona fide Puerto Rico resident who excludes WAGES at line 2a and happens to own a MAINLAND farm: a return this dictionary computes correctly today. That is the same shape scheduleA:/possessionUnapportionedCharitableCarryover records for condition (ii) ("testing answered-ness rather than a non-zero amount"), one degree worse, because (ii) at least discharges when someone apportions the carryover while this one discharges only when a new intake is built. IT IS STILL THE RIGHT TRADE: the alternative is an undisclosed taxpayer-FAVOURABLE leak in two places at once, on a population the graph can see. Stated here rather than found later.
WORLD-1: additive, and MEASURED rather than argued. THE THIRD ARM MOVES NONE OF THE 969: `grep -rl writableRoyaltyIsWorkingInterest scenarios/` returns nothing, so no committed scenario answers the working-interest writable at all and the fact's Complete-true count over the materialized corpus is unchanged at four. NONE of the four moves the knockout: ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion appears NOWHERE in this unit's delta file , which is the mechanical proof that the outer All short-circuited on all four — they answer no Schedule 8812 line 2a or 2c entry. That is the short-circuit claim above, checked across the whole corpus rather than on one fixture.

Fact.Name: The return excludes self-employment income, so the Pub. 570 fraction applies
Fact.Description:
The gate on the apportioned arms of /selfEmploymentTaxOnNonexcludedIncome and /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction: TRUE only when a non-zero section 931/933 exclusion is reported against a Schedule C AND the fraction's denominator is usable.
THE IDENTITY IT BUYS IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN ARITHMETICAL, which is the same reason standardDeduction:/hasPossessionExclusionProration exists: a return that excludes nothing takes the FULL deduction by taking a different arm, not by multiplying by a fraction that happens to equal one.
MEMBER ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS A COMPLETENESS GUARD, not a style choice. The exclusion test comes FIRST because scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit is Complete $0 on every return by its own double guard, and All short-circuits to Complete(false) — so on every committed return this fact is Complete false WITHOUT ever evaluating the denominator, whose two Schedule SE line-3 addends can be Incomplete on a refused return. The IsComplete member then stands between the short-circuit and the GreaterThan for the returns that do get past it. Reordering these three members can turn /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction Placeholder on a refused return, which is the exact trap /netEarningsFromSelfEmployment's COMPLETENESS DESIGN paragraph records.
DELIBERATELY NOT A DEPENDENCY ON ctcOdc:/knockoutPossessionOrPuertoRicoIncomeExclusion, and deliberately NOT keyed on the Schedule 8812 line 2a/2c entries the way standardDeduction:/hasPossessionExclusionProration is. This is the SELF-EMPLOYMENT fraction, so its precondition is that self-employment income was excluded — which only the per-Schedule-C intake says. A filer who excludes wages at line 2a and no business income apportions nothing here, correctly.

Fact.Name: Self-employment tax on nonexcluded income (Pub. 570 chapter 4)
Fact.Description:
The publication's own named intermediate: "figure the self-employment tax on the nonexcluded income by multiplying your total self-employment tax (from Schedule SE (Form 1040)) by the following fraction ... The result is your self-employment tax on nonexcluded income." It exists as a fact rather than as an inline product BECAUSE the publication names it and takes half of it in a separate sentence; collapsing the two steps would hide which half of the rule a future correction is touching.
EQUAL TO /selfEmploymentTax ON EVERY RETURN THAT EXCLUDES NOTHING, by taking the fall-through arm rather than by multiplying by one.
⚠ IT IS NOT A TAX ANYONE OWES. Schedule 2 line 4 still carries the whole /selfEmploymentTax: section 1402(a)(6) leaves the excluded income in the self-employment tax base, and this quantity exists "for purposes of the deduction only" — the publication's own four words. Nothing but /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction reads it, and nothing else should.
THE FOUR-DECIMAL RATIO IDIOM is standardDeduction:/standardDeduction's, used at the same scale and for the same reason: the engine has no fixed-point ratio type, so the quotient is multiplied by 10,000, RoundToInt yields the four-decimal ratio as an integer, and the product is divided back by 10,000. The two 10,000s cancel exactly and neither is a tax parameter. WHAT IS INFERRED RATHER THAN PRINTED, stated because it is a real gap: this sentence says only "by the following fraction" and never says "to four decimals". The four decimals are carried over from the chapter's GROSS-income fraction, whose worked example does present itself that way — a different rule on the same page. An exact-arithmetic reading would differ by cents on some returns and there is no published number to adjudicate it. interpretation:provisional.
THE DENOMINATOR GUARD IS ON /hasSelfEmploymentExclusionProration, which requires it strictly positive, so the Divide below can never see a zero divisor.

Fact.Name: Full deduction for one-half of self-employment tax, before the Pub. 570 apportionment
Fact.Description:
The two filers' Schedule SE line 13s added — i.e. exactly the un-apportioned body of /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction, extracted UNCHANGED so the apportioned amount has an un-apportioned twin to stand against.
TWO REASONS IT IS A FACT AND NOT AN INLINED ARM, and the second is the load-bearing one: 1. It is the fall-through arm of /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction, so extracting it makes the identity on a non-excluding return visible as one dependency rather than as a repeated body. 2. IT IS THE SUBTRAHEND /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome NOW READS BY NAME. That fact used to read /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction, and re-bodying that path would have moved it SILENTLY — a smaller subtrahend against an unchanged minuend RAISES EIC and ACTC earned income, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, and unintended. Pointing it here is what stops that; see that fact's own CHOSEN READING paragraph for why the pair stays put.
NOT AN EXPORT SURFACE FOR SCHEDULE 1. Form 1040 Schedule 1 line 15 is the APPORTIONED figure — "Include the deductible part of this amount on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15" is the publication's own sentence about the apportioned quantity — so /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction remains the MeF-exported line and this fact is a building block beneath it. The same two-step shape standardDeduction:/fullStandardDeduction takes, for the same printed reason.
interpretation:provisional — the per-Schedule-SE rounding convention is inherited verbatim from /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction and is documented there.

Fact.Name: Deduction for one-half of self-employment tax
Fact.Description:
The return's total Schedule SE line 13: each filer's own half, computed and rounded on that filer's own Schedule SE, then added — the above-the-line adjustment on Schedule 1 line 15 that reduces AGI. interpretation:provisional — CHOSEN READING: round each half on its own Schedule SE, then add (Add(Round(0.5 x pLine12), Round(0.5 x sLine12))), because line 13 is a line ON a Schedule SE and each spouse files a separate one; the addition happens later, at Schedule 1 line 15. REJECTED: halve the combined line 12 (Round(0.5 x (pLine12 + sLine12))), which is what a single-chain model computes and which differs by $1 whenever BOTH line 12s are odd. The two readings are indistinguishable on every return with only one Schedule SE, so this choice is only observable on a joint return with SE income on both sides — a node test of a joint return where both filers have their own wage base is drawn (6,237 and 14,131, both odd) specifically to make it observable and pin it at 10,185 rather than 10,184. ⚠ THAT REJECTION IS SCOPED TO THE UN-APPORTIONED ARM, AND IS NOT WITHDRAWN. It governs /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction, which is the whole of this fact's body on every return that excludes nothing — i.e. every committed return, and every return that node test describes. The APPORTIONED arm below halves a RETURN-LEVEL amount and therefore does the thing that paragraph rejects, deliberately, because Publication 570 chapter 4 says to: its multiplicand is "your TOTAL self-employment tax (from Schedule SE (Form 1040))" and its output is one Schedule 1 line 15 figure, so the rule is stated at the return level and there is no per-Schedule-SE fraction to take. The alternative construction — apportion each filer's own rounded line 13 — is within a cent and has no printed sentence; it is not chosen, and no vendored number adjudicates between them.
REBODIED INTO A TWO-ARM SWITCH, and this is the SCHEDULE 1 LINE 15 FIGURE. Publication 570 chapter 4 apportions this deduction for a filer who excludes part of their self-employment income under section 931 or 933 — "Include the deductible part of this amount on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15" — so the apportionment belongs INSIDE this path rather than beside it, which is why this fact was re-bodied and no consumer was re-pointed. Arm 1 (gated on /hasSelfEmploymentExclusionProration): one-half of /selfEmploymentTaxOnNonexcludedIncome. Arm 2: /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction, byte-identical to the body that shipped before, taken structurally rather than by a fraction equal to one.
THE THREE CONSUMERS ALL FOLLOW, CORRECTLY, and each was walked rather than assumed: • taxCalculations:/allowableAdjustmentsToIncome — Schedule 1 line 15 itself, which is the line the publication names. This is the "directly related adjustments" limb of Publication 1321's caution, and it is now built. • ctcOdc:/socialSecurityOverEitc — Schedule 8812 line 22's Schedule 1 line 15 term. Line 22 asks for the amount ON that line, so the apportioned figure is the one it wants. DIRECTION of the change for this population: a smaller line 22 lowers the section 24(d)(2) social-security comparison, which can only REDUCE a Part II-B additional child tax credit — taxpayer-adverse, and it is the arithmetic the statute describes rather than a residual. • ctcOdc:/sched8812Line21's sibling arithmetic reads /socialSecurityTaxesWithheld, not this path, and is unaffected. ONE CONSUMER DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FOLLOW: /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome, which now names /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction. Its reasoning is on that fact. ⚠ A FOURTH CONSUMER EXISTS AND IT DOES FOLLOW: /selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax, the Schedule 8812 line-18a twin of /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome. So the pair is now symmetric and each half is worksheet-sourced rather than argued: the Schedule 8812 Earned Income Worksheet line 5 says "Enter the amount from Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15" — THIS fact — while EIC Worksheet B Part 1 line 1d says "Enter the amount from Schedule SE, Part I, line 13" — /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction. Two worksheets, two subtrahends, one per consumer. The "THREE CONSUMERS" heading above is superseded by this paragraph; it is four, three following and one deliberately not.
⚠⚠ THE INCOME SIDE HAS NOT MOVED, SO THIS CUT LANDS ON INCOME THE RETURN STILL TAXES. income:/totalIncome reads scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit — the COMBINED line 31 — and this unit does not change it (income.xml is untouched; the seven-consumer deferral list is on scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax). So a filer who answers the per-item exclusion intake is taxed on the excluded profit AND loses the deduction allocable to it. Under section 933 properly applied the filer would be taxed on 40,000 and take 2,826. DIRECTION: COMPOUNDING TAXPAYER-ADVERSE. It is the safer class and it has precedent under the same condition — a sibling unit prorates the standard deduction and the possession-income intake work closes the QBI admission gate, both while total income still carries the excluded profit — but it is not a rounding residual and it is stated here rather than left to be discovered. Publication 1321's disallowance is conditioned on "if you are excluding", and on this tree the filer's income tax does not yet reflect the exclusion. CONDITION (v) DOES NOT DETECT IT. scheduleC:/possessionUntreatedScheduleCNetProfit fires on the UNANSWERED intake; this is the ANSWERED case, which is exactly the return that computes. IT DISCHARGES WHEN income:/totalIncome MOVES to scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax, which is the remaining half of the possession-income review's list. This fact and qbi:/qbiAutoDerivedAmount are the first two that make the compounding OBSERVABLE, which is why the paragraph lives on them. ⚠⚠ DISCHARGED BY THE POSSESSION APPORTIONMENT'S SECOND STEP — the block above is the record of the defect between the two steps and every clause of it is now false. income:/totalIncome reads scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax, so the SAME return the block traces now taxes 40,000 rather than 100,000 while Schedule 1 line 15 stays at 2,826 — which is exactly the "under section 933 properly applied" sentence above, reached. The compounding is gone: the deduction cut here now lands on income the return no longer taxes. The other three income-side consumers moved with it and two deliberately did not; the table is on scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax.
THE PER-FILER SIBLINGS ARE NOT APPORTIONED, and the residual is UNSIGNED rather than disclosed in one direction. /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction and /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction keep their full line 13s, so /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncome and its sibling — Form 2441's per-spouse earned income and the section 219(b)(1)(B) IRA compensation ceiling — subtract too MUCH (adverse) from a Schedule SE line 3 that still contains the excluded income (favourable), and nothing vendored says which dominates. Form 2441's own item 2 says "minus any deduction you claim on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15", which after this unit is the APPORTIONED amount, so the printed sentence points at moving them; Publication 590-A and Publication 503 say nothing about section 931/933 at all, so the minuend has no printed answer and moving one half alone is the defect the possession-income review was opened to prevent. They are left whole and named here. NOTE this is a SECOND reason the per-filer and return-level facts diverge, beside the per-filer earned-income split's per-spouse one. THE qbi PRORATION IS UNAFFECTED BY THAT CHOICE AND MUST STAY SO: qbi:/scheduleCs/*/qbiAttributableHalfSeTax multiplies the FULL per-filer line 13 by the item's NONEXCLUDED profit over the owner's whole line-3 base, which is algebraically the apportioned share already. Apportioning the per-filer facts as well would apply the fraction twice. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (Schedule CA (540), Schedule CA (540NR)).

Fact.Name: Net self-employment earned income
Fact.Description:
Self-employment earned income for credit purposes: Schedule C net profit plus the Schedule K-1 box 14 code A partnership SE earnings (scheduleE:/k1SeEarnings, signed, complete-safe 0) plus the Schedule F line 34 net farm profit or loss (scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss, signed, complete-safe 0), minus the deductible half of SE tax, SIGNED — EIC Worksheet B line 1a is Schedule SE line 3, which includes the K-1 amount and, since Schedule SE line 1a was wired, the farm amount too. THE FARM ADDEND IS NOT OPTIONAL AND THE REASON IS ARITHMETIC, not tidiness. The SUBTRAHEND of this Subtract, /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction is the sum of the two per-filer Schedule SE line 13s, and those grew the moment the farm term joined line 3. Adding the farm to line 3 WITHOUT adding it here would have moved the subtrahend while leaving the minuend alone: a farm profit would have REDUCED a filer's EITC earned income and a farm loss would have RAISED it, both backwards, and neither error existed before the farm was wired. The node test scheduleSE/se1a-farm-profit-raises-se-tax asserts this fact for that reason. DELIBERATELY return-level, not per-filer: EIC Worksheet B is computed for the return (a joint return's earned income is both spouses'), so this reads the aggregate /k1SeEarnings and the aggregate /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction rather than either per-filer chain. CONSUMERS: the EITC earned-income facts ONLY. Form 2441 and the IRA worksheet are PER-SPOUSE surfaces, so the CDCC earned-income facts and the IRA-deduction compensation bases read /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncome and /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncome below. Do not add a per-spouse consumer to this fact — that is the per-filer earned-income split defect.
⚠ SECTION 931/933: NEITHER HALF MOVES, AND THAT IS A CHOSEN READING RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE OF ONE. This fact is (Schedule C net profit + K-1 + farm) MINUS the deductible half of self-employment tax, and the possession-income review proved the two halves must move together or not at all: moving the minuend alone understates EIC and ACTC earned income, moving the subtrahend alone overstates it. This unit takes the "or not at all" arm on BOTH — the minuend stays scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit (the combined line 31) and the subtrahend is pinned BY NAME to /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction, which is what stops the re-body of /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction from moving this fact silently in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction. ⚠ RE-EXAMINED AND RE-AFFIRMED WHEN income:/totalIncome DID MOVE. Fact.Name: Net self-employment earned income taken into account in computing taxable income (Schedule 8812 line 18a)
Fact.Description:
THE SECTION 24(d) TWIN of /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome above (condition (B), the line-18a gap). Same three addends and the same floor; TWO substitutions, and each has its own printed authority: • the MINUEND reads scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax — the NONEXCLUDED Schedule C line 31 — where /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome reads the combined scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit; • the SUBTRAHEND reads /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction — Schedule 1 line 15, the Publication 570 chapter 4 APPORTIONED half — where /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome reads /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction, the whole Schedule SE line 13. Both moves are in the SAME direction only in the sense that both shrink; they push the DIFFERENCE opposite ways, so the net fall is the excluded profit LESS the disallowed part of the half-SE-tax deduction. On this unit's witness: 92,935 becomes 37,174, which is (100,000 - 60,000) - 2,826 rather than 92,935 - 60,000.
WHY THE SPLIT IS REQUIRED RATHER THAN CHOSEN, which is what the possession-income review and the possession apportionment could not settle and what closes it. The two consumers of the old shared path have two DIFFERENT STATUTES and they point opposite ways, both in printed text: • EITC — section 32(c)(2)(A)(ii) takes "the amount of the taxpayer's net earnings from self-employment for the taxable year (within the meaning of section 1402(a))", and section 1402(a) puts BOTH exclusions back in: paragraph (6) computes a Puerto Rico resident's net earnings "without regard to section 933" and paragraph (9) says "the exclusion from gross income provided by section 931 shall not apply". So the excluded profit IS EITC earned income, and /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome is right to keep it. • ACTC — section 24(d)(1)(B)(i) takes "so much of the taxpayer's earned income (within the meaning of section 32) WHICH IS TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT IN COMPUTING TAXABLE INCOME for the taxable year as exceeds" the floor. That clause is a SECOND filter applied on top of the section 32 amount, and income excluded from gross income under section 931 or 933 is not taken into account in computing taxable income. So the excluded profit is NOT line-18a earned income. The clause is not a stray reading: section 24(d)(1)'s own flush language has to carve combat pay BACK IN — "any amount excluded from gross income by reason of section 112 shall be treated as earned income which is taken into account in computing taxable income for the taxable year" — which would be surplusage if excluded income were already inside. This dictionary already implements that carve-in, at income:/earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay's formW2s:/allCombatPay addend. (The surplusage inference is this unit's, not printed.)
THE IRS APPLIES THE CLAUSE IN TWO PLACES, AND ONE OF THEM IS NOT PUERTO-RICO-SPECIFIC — which is what dissolves the possession-income review's second blocker (that the printed sentence names Puerto Rico while the intake scheduleC:/scheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit does not separate section 933 from section 931): • under the "Bona Fide Residents of Puerto Rico" heading, "On line 18a, include only earned income you reported on Form 1040 or 1040-SR. Don't include income earned in Puerto Rico, which you exclude from U.S. tax as a bona fide resident of Puerto Rico" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 3 continuing at lines 147-149, a sentence that splits across a two-column extraction); • in the GENERAL Line 18a instruction, with no residency heading over it, "Income excluded under a tax treaty is ALSO excluded from the computation of earned income on line 18a" (same file, lines 172-173). The word "also" presupposes that other excluded income is already out, which is the statutory clause showing through. SO THIS FACT IS NOT GATED ON ctcOdc:/isBonaFidePuertoRicoResident and does not separate the two exclusion sections. The possession-income review's third blocker (residency-conditioning) dissolves the same way: section 24(d)(1)(B)(i) is residency-agnostic, and the instruction's heading is where the IRS puts the common case, not a condition on the statute. Gating on residency would leave a section 931 filer's excluded profit inside line 18a with nothing to say for it.
WHY THE SUBTRAHEND MOVES TOO, and it is the half most easily got wrong. The two worksheets that figure these two quantities name DIFFERENT LINES for the same deduction: • EIC Worksheet B Part 1 line 1d — "Enter the amount from Schedule SE, Part I, line 13" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf, page 47), i.e. the FULL half, which is /fullSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction; • the Schedule 8812 Earned Income Worksheet line 5 — "Enter the amount from Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040s8.pdf, page 8), which after the possession apportionment step 1 is the APPORTIONED half, /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction. A bona fide resident of Puerto Rico cannot claim the EITC at all ("Bona fide residents of Puerto Rico cannot claim the Earned Income Tax Credit", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1321.pdf, page 7), so this population takes the Earned Income Chart's "are not taking the EIC" row straight to the Earned Income Worksheet — the Schedule 1 line 15 route. The statute agrees by a second road: section 32(c)(2)(A)(ii) says the net earnings are determined "with regard to the deduction ALLOWED to the taxpayer by section 164(f)", and for this filer the deduction ALLOWED is the apportioned one, because section 933(1) disallows the part allocable to excluded income. A section 931 filer who IS taking the EIC routes to Worksheet B instead; the routing then differs but the arithmetic this fact performs does not, because Worksheet B's own minuend (Schedule SE line 3) is not what line 18a asks for. CORRECTION THIS CARRIES: /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome's Description said "EIC Worksheet B and Form 2441 both define the subtrahend as 'any deduction you claim on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15'". That is true of Form 2441 and FALSE of EIC Worksheet B, whose line 1d names Schedule SE line 13. The claim is corrected on that fact; the conclusion it was used for (keep the full deduction on the EITC leg) is UNCHANGED and is now better supported than the sentence that was making it.
⚠ A THIRD SUBSTITUTION: a SECOND SUBTRAHEND, scheduleC:/statutoryEmployeeScheduleCNetProfit, which is Earned Income Worksheet LINE 2b's exclusion of statutory employee income from the Schedule C line 31 collection. The EIC twin /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome got the same rule in a DIFFERENT shape - it swapped its minuend to the gated per filer Schedule C totals - and that shape is unavailable here because this fact's minuend carries the section 931/933 exclusion, which has no per filer partition. Same rule, two shapes, and the reason each is what it is sits on both facts so a later reader does not "harmonise" them into a double subtraction. The add-back half, worksheet line 2a, is the fourth addend of income:/earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay. Complete safe $0, so no committed line 18a moves.
COMPLETENESS: THE CONE DOES NOT WIDEN PAST /agi, which is what keeps this additive on the delta store. The two substituted dependencies are both already inside the adjusted-gross- income cone on EVERY return — income:/totalIncome reads scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitSubjectToUsTax and taxCalculations:/allowableAdjustmentsToIncome reads /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction — so a case on which either could be Incomplete is a case on which AGI is already Incomplete.
WHAT IS STILL TOO LARGE HERE, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE and unchanged by this unit: the K-1 box 14 code A and Schedule F addends are read WHOLE, because no intake exists for excluded territory self-employment income arriving that way. That is the same gap /selfEmploymentIncomeSubjectToUsTax discloses for the Publication 570 fraction, and it now leaks through Schedule 8812 line 18a as well. Detected, for the unasked-Schedule-C case only, by scheduleC:/possessionUntreatedScheduleCNetProfit.
THE TRADER AND COMMUNITY TERMS. Earned Income Worksheet line 2b leaves out "any other amounts exempt from self-employment tax", so the section 1402(a)(3) trader carve-out (/primaryFilerScheduleSeTraderScheduleCExclusionAsCombined) is read here as on the EIC twin. That term negates the UNEXCLUDED primary Schedule C profit while this minuend holds only the nonexcluded part, so /primaryFilerScheduleSeTraderExcludedTerritoryAddBack restores the excluded share once; without it an excluding trader's excluded profit would leave twice. The worksheet's instruction to disregard community property laws is what the two Schedule SE line 3 community-income entries implement, so /primaryFilerScheduleSeCommunityIncomeAdjustmentAsCombined is read too, and like the EIC twin this fact is Incomplete on a freed community-property return that has not answered them.

Fact.Name: Schedule 8812 Earned Income Worksheet line 2e (net farm profit or loss after the farm optional method)
Fact.Description:
Line 2e of the Schedule 8812 Earned Income Worksheet, the farm term of /selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax (Schedule 8812 line 18a). • Line 2c is the net farm profit or loss from Schedule F line 34 (scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss). • Line 2d applies only when the farm optional method was used, and is Schedule SE line 15: /farmOptionalMethodNetEarningsApplied for the primary filer plus, on a joint return, /secondaryFilerFarmOptionalMethodNetEarningsApplied. Each is already capped at the $7,240 line 14 ceiling and is $0 for a filer who did not elect. • Line 2e: when some filer used the farm optional method and line 2c is a profit, the smaller of line 2c or line 2d; otherwise line 2c, loss included. So the farm optional method can only LOWER this term, never raise it above the actual Schedule F profit. Without it, a filer who elected the method on a farm whose line 15 is below its Schedule F profit carried the whole profit into line 18a, which overstated the refundable child tax credit base.
The election gate is load-bearing. Both applied amounts default to $0 when there is no election, so the smaller-of rule without the gate would zero every Schedule F profit.
DISCLOSED LIMIT. Line 2c also takes farm partnership Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A. This dictionary holds box 14 code A as one farm-and-nonfarm figure (scheduleE:/k1SeEarnings), read whole beside this term. So a farm K-1 share never enters the smaller-of comparison here. With a farm K-1 profit this term is at most the amount the worksheet would give, and the smaller-of rule is simply not applied to that share.
Complete wherever Schedule F line 34 is. Both election flags are complete-safe, and the joint-return test is guarded by IsComplete.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's net self-employment earned income, floored at zero (eligibility screen)
Fact.Description: The PRIMARY filer's self-employment earned income for the CDCC eligibility screen: HIS Schedule SE line 3 (/primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss — his own attributed Schedule C net profit plus his own box-14A K-1 earnings) less HIS OWN Schedule 1 line 15 deduction (/primaryFilerSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction), floored at zero. Deliberately does NOT read the return-level /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome, which mixes both spouses' figures: Form 2441's earned-income limitation is per spouse (§21(d)(1) takes the SMALLER of the two), so a return-level amount booked on one side moves that minimum and computes the wrong credit. Value-identical to the return-level fact on every non-MFJ return and on every joint return with no secondary-filer self-employment, because the secondary chain is then complete-safe 0 on both terms. interpretation:provisional — CHOSEN READING: the zero floor is applied PER FILER, on this filer's own line 3 less his own line 13, so one spouse's self-employment loss never reduces the other's earned income. REJECTED: floor the combined figure once and split it, which is what reading the return-level fact on both sides amounts to, and which the per-Schedule-SE "figure ... separately" instruction forbids. THE FLOOR IS DELIBERATE HERE AND the floor-versus-loss adjudication ADJUDICATED IT (the caveat this Description used to carry is discharged, not carried forward). The per-filer earned-income split disclosed that Form 2441's CAUTION — "You must reduce your earned income by any loss from self-employment" — is incompatible with a floored figure, and filed the floor-versus-loss adjudication to settle it. The floor-versus-loss adjudication found the two consumers want OPPOSITE treatments, on two authorities that each say so in one sentence: • Form 2441 / CDCC: the loss REDUCES earned income (Pub. 503, "Net loss") — so the four Form 2441 amount lines now read the UNFLOORED siblings /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncomeNetOfLoss and /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncomeNetOfLoss below. • IRA compensation: the loss does NOT reduce wages (Pub. 590-A, "Self-employment loss. If you have a net loss from self-employment, don't subtract the loss from your salaries or wages when figuring your total compensation"). IRA uses the separate /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncomeForIraCompensation below, which keeps this zero floor and removes the §1402(a)(8) minister add-back under IRC 401(c)(2)(A)(iv). CONSUMER OF THIS FLOORED FACT: cdcc:/maybeEligibleForCdccBase's self-employment arm (a > 0 eligibility SCREEN, where floored-at-0 and a negative both fail the test, so the screen's value is identical either way — see the disclosure on that fact). Form 2441's amount lines read the unfloored /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncomeNetOfLoss sibling. This fact keeps the Schedule SE add-back IN, as the Form 2441 line-3 formula requires.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's net self-employment earned income, floored at zero (eligibility screen)
