Before the per-filer earned-income split this quantity did not exist and the consumers had no secondary self-employment term at all, so a spouse whose only earned income was her business read $0 on her side of the §21(d)(1) minimum and the CDCC collapsed. Complete-safe 0 on a non-MFJ return and on every joint return with no secondary-filer self-employment. interpretation:provisional — same CHOSEN/REJECTED pair as /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncome (per-filer floor, not a split of a combined one). The floor-vs-loss caveat the per-filer earned-income split disclosed here is DISCHARGED by the floor-versus-loss adjudication on the same terms as the primary sibling: the Form 2441 amount lines moved to /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncomeNetOfLoss (Pub. 503's "Net loss" reduces earned income). The IRA module instead reads /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncomeForIraCompensation below; that sibling keeps the §219 zero floor and removes the section 1402(a)(8) add-back under section 401(c)(2)(A)(iv). This fact keeps the Schedule SE add-back IN, as Form 2441's line-3 formula requires.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's net self-employment earned income for IRA compensation, floored at zero
Fact.Description: Primary-filer self-employment compensation under IRC 219(f)(1) and 401(c)(2)(A)(iv): HIS Schedule SE line 3 (/primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss) less HIS Schedule 1 line 15 deduction (/primaryFilerSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction) and the section 1402(a)(8) minister housing-and-meals add-back (/primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack), floored at zero. The minister subtraction prevents Schedule SE's required add-back for §1402(a) from inflating the §219(b)(1)(B) IRA compensation ceiling. Two further terms follow the statute where line 3 does not: the ministerial net earnings an approved Form 4361 excludes from line 3 (/primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined, negated) are added back, because IRC 401(c)(2)(A)(ii) figures earned income without regard to section 1402(c)(4) and (5); and his Schedule C profit excluded from gross income under section 931 or 933 on Form 4563 (scheduleC:/primaryFilerScheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit) is taken out, because compensation is what is includible in gross income (IRC 219(b)(1)(B), 401(c)(2)(A)(iv)). His ministerial W-2 salary on line 2 (/primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterW2SalaryIncluded) is taken out too: it is W-2 box 1 wages, which the IRA Deduction Worksheet counts on line 8, and line 9 is the earned income received as a self-employed individual, so the salary counts once. Like the original floored fact, a self-employment loss does not reduce wages. Complete-safe 0 when the primary filer has no Schedule SE earnings; follows the minister add-back's Incomplete posture when the filer has answered the minister gate but left required details unanswered. Foreign-government or international-organization wages on line 2 (/primaryFilerScheduleSeForeignGovernmentEmployeeIncomeIncluded) are taken out the same way (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-308, mirroring AD-30): they are wages includible in gross income, which Pub. 590-A counts as compensation ("Wages, salaries, tips, professional fees, bonuses, and other amounts you receive for providing personal services", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p590a.pdf, page 6), so they count once, on worksheet line 8. The half-SE-tax deduction stays subtracted in full, as for the minister's salary; whether only the trade-or-business share should reduce other self-employment earnings is open (IN-308, with AD-30).

Fact.Description: The secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentEarnedIncomeForIraCompensation: HER own Schedule SE line 3 less HER Schedule 1 line 15 deduction and her section 1402(a)(8) minister housing-and-meals add-back, plus the ministerial net earnings her approved Form 4361 excludes from line 3 (IRC 401(c)(2)(A)(ii)), less her section 931/933 excluded Schedule C profit (scheduleC:/secondaryFilerScheduleCExcludedTerritoryNetProfit) and her ministerial W-2 salary on line 2, which is W-2 box 1 wages counted on IRA Deduction Worksheet line 8, floored at zero. The half-SE-tax deduction stays subtracted in full, as for the minister's salary; whether only the trade-or-business share should reduce other self-employment earnings is open (IN-308, with AD-30).

Fact.Name: Primary filer's net self-employment earned income, loss NOT floored (Form 2441 line 4 / line 18)

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 1b as line 3 combines it, the negated Conservation Reserve Program payments, complete safe
Fact.Description:
The Schedule SE line 1b entry as the printed line 3 combines it: $0 minus /writableScheduleSeLine1bConservationReservePayments when that intake was answered, and $0 otherwise.
WHY IT IS NEGATED HERE RATHER THAN SUBTRACTED THERE. The printed 1b box is a parentheses field and the intake is entered as a POSITIVE amount, while line 3 reads "Combine lines 1a, 1b, and 2". Negating at this one place means /primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss stays a literal Add of the three printed lines, in the same shape income:/schedule1Line8aNetOperatingLossDeduction already uses for the parenthesised Schedule 1 line 8a. A reader who negates it again restores the payments to earnings.
WHY IT IS COMPLETE SAFE. The intake is a bare Writable, so a raw Dependency on it would make line 3, line 4a, the self-employment tax, the SE tax deduction and AGI Incomplete on every return that is not a farm return, which is nearly all of them.
WHAT CHANGED IN THE TAX. IRC 1402(a)(1) excludes Conservation Reserve Program payments from net earnings from self-employment for an individual receiving social security retirement or disability benefits. Before this fact existed the payments never reduced net earnings, which is the OVER-taxing direction /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1a disclosed for the missing line 1b; that disclosure is now closed for the line 3 arithmetic. $0 on every committed scenario, so no scenario moved.
THE EXCLUSION HAS A CONDITION AND THE CONDITION IS NOW ASKED. IRC 1402(a)(1) excludes the payments only for "individuals receiving benefits under section 202 or 223 of the Social Security Act", and the printed line says the same in the filer's own terms: "If you received social security retirement or disability benefits, enter the amount ...". /writableScheduleSeLine1bReceivingSocialSecurityBenefits carries that attestation. A return that enters a CRP amount against THIS chain's farm and leaves the attestation blank resolves this fact INCOMPLETE - no arm matches - rather than granting the reduction: an unanswered condition of allowance on a return that claims the allowance is a refusal, not a default. The refusal is exactly as wide as the condition: whether the farm is this chain's is decided without the attestation, so the other spouse's twin still resolves a Complete $0. A return that enters nothing on line 1b never sees the question and stays complete-safe $0.
WHOSE SCHEDULE SE: the filer whose farm it is. The payments are the ones "included on Schedule F, line 4b", and this dictionary models one farm, so they follow that farm's attribution (scheduleF:/scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler) exactly as line 1a does. When the farm is the spouse's this fact is $0 and /secondaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bAsCombined carries the reduction instead.
EXCEPT ON A QUALIFIED JOINT VENTURE, where the farm is BOTH spouses' and there is no owner to route by. An elected QJV takes its own arm, ahead of the attribution arm, and books /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bCrpQjvShare - the entered amount times the respective interest - while the secondary twin books the remainder. The attribution arm carries Not(scheduleF:/scheduleFIsQualifiedJointVenture) so it cannot fire on a QJV: /scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler resolves Complete TRUE on a QJV return whose owner question was never asked (its fall-through is a literal True), so without that conjunct the whole reduction would land on the primary filer with nothing asking and nothing blocking. IRC 761(f)(1)(B) divides "all items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit", and this exclusion is one of them.
WHAT IS STILL OWED, and it is NOT this fact's to close: the farm versus nonfarm Schedule K-1 box 14 code A discriminator that /writableScheduleSeLine1bConservationReservePayments names, because a CRP amount listed in K-1 box 20 code AQ belongs to a FARM partnership whose box 14 code A this dictionary routes to line 2. That affects which printed line the partnership earnings land on, not whether line 3 subtracts the CRP amount, which is what this fact does. A K-1 box 20 code AQ amount also follows the K-1's OWN filer rather than the farm's, which this fact cannot yet distinguish from a Schedule F line 4b amount. interpretation:provisional.

WHY IT EXISTS. IRC 761(f)(1)(B) divides "all items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit" between the spouses, not just the net profit, and the CRP exclusion is one of those items. Before this fact the whole reduction followed scheduleF:/scheduleFBelongsToPrimaryFiler, which a qualified joint venture election does not move and which falls through to the PRIMARY filer on an unanswered owner question - a question a QJV return is never asked, since the farm belongs to both spouses.
INCOMPLETE WHENEVER THE SPLIT IS, and never $0 by default: it multiplies scheduleF:/scheduleFQjvPrimaryFilerInterestAsRational, which refuses on a non-QJV return, on a blank percentage and on a percentage outside the 1 to 99 band. Both readers guard it - each reads it only from an arm that has already established the election, an entered CRP amount and an affirmative benefits attestation - so the Incomplete it resolves on every ordinary return never reaches a Schedule SE.

Fact.Name: Were you receiving social security retirement or disability benefits when the CRP payments arrived?
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Were you receiving Social Security retirement or disability benefits at the time you received your Conservation Reserve Program payments?" HELP TEXT: only a farmer who was already drawing those benefits may leave CRP payments out of self-employment earnings; everyone else pays self-employment tax on them. Answer yes only if the benefits had started by the time each payment arrived. This is about Social Security retirement or disability benefits, not Supplemental Security Income and not a railroad or state pension (2025 Instructions for Schedule SE, Line 1b; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 3). ASKED WHEN: the filer entered an amount on Schedule SE line 1b (/writableScheduleSeLine1bConservationReservePayments); the question is never shown to a return with no CRP entry. On a joint return it is asked of the spouse whose farm this is, which scheduleF:/writableScheduleFBelongsToSecondaryFiler already establishes. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED - a return that entered a CRP amount and left this blank cannot be finished, because /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bAsCombined (or its secondary twin) resolves Incomplete and carries that through line 3, the self-employment tax and AGI. It is not defaulted either way: defaulting YES would grant an exclusion the filer never claimed the condition for, and defaulting NO would silently discard an entry the filer did make. Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 3 notary-public adjustment, negated, complete safe
Fact.Description:
The Schedule SE line-3 dotted-line notary adjustment as line 3 combines it: $0 minus /writableScheduleSeNotaryPublicNetProfit when that intake was answered, and $0 otherwise. The exact idiom /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bAsCombined already uses for the line 1b CRP subtraction, applied to the notary exclusion.
WHY IT IS NEGATED HERE RATHER THAN SUBTRACTED THERE. The printed instruction reads "enter 'Exempt—Notary' and the amount of your net profit as a notary public from Schedule C on the dotted line to the left of Schedule SE, line 3. Subtract that amount from the total of lines 1a, 1b, and 2, and enter the result on line 3." Negating at this one place lets /primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss stay a literal Add of the line-3 components, the same shape the line-1b term already uses. A reader who negates it again restores the notary profit to earnings.
WHY IT IS COMPLETE SAFE. The intake is a bare Writable, so a raw Dependency on it would make line 3, line 4a, self-employment tax, the SE tax deduction and AGI Incomplete on every return that does not answer the notary screen, which is nearly all of them.
WHAT CHANGED IN THE TAX. IRC 1402(c)(1) excludes "the performance of the functions of a public office ... compensated solely on a fee basis" from the trade-or-business definition that net earnings from self-employment is built on, and both the Schedule SE instructions and Publication 334 say plainly that notary fees, though reported on Schedule C, are not subject to SE tax. Before this fact existed, a notary's net profit was taxed on Schedule SE exactly like any other Schedule C profit — an OVER-taxing gap this fact closes for the line 3 arithmetic. $0 on every committed scenario, so no scenario moves.
THIS TERM ALSO REACHES THE TWO EITC/ACTC EARNED-INCOME TWINS (/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome and /selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax), which reconstruct Schedule SE line 3 rather than reading it, because EIC Worksheet B Part 2's own instruction says "Don't include on these lines any ... net profit from services performed as a notary public" — the same exclusion Worksheet B Part 1 line 1a gets for free by reading Schedule SE line 3 directly.
WHOSE SCHEDULE SE: the PRIMARY filer's, matching this module's unqualified-path convention. A secondary-filer twin is owed whenever the MFJ two-Schedules-SE gap closes. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 3 — notary public net profit excluded from self-employment tax
Fact.Description:
The Schedule SE Part I dotted-line adjustment beside line 3, asking how much of the filer's Schedule C net profit came from services performed as a notary public.
QUESTION TEXT: "How much of your self-employment net profit was from work you did as a notary public?" HELP TEXT: "Fees you receive for acting as a notary public are reported on Schedule C, but the tax code excludes the performance of a public office compensated on a fee basis from self-employment tax, and the IRS confirms notary fees are not subject to SE tax (Instructions for Schedule SE, 'Income and Losses Not Included in Net Earnings From Self-Employment,' item 2; Pub. 334, 'Notary public'). The exclusion is FUNCTIONAL, not a whole-business label: it reaches only the fees you earned performing notarial acts themselves (taking acknowledgments, administering oaths, certifying copies), not a broader signing-agent or document-preparation business you run on the same Schedule C even if you are also a notary — enter only the notarial-act share, not your whole signing-agent or document-preparation profit. Enter the part of your Schedule C net profit that came from notary work; leave this blank if you had no notary income." ASKED-WHEN: after the filer's Schedule C income is entered, on a screen reachable whenever the filer has any Schedule C net profit (the amount cannot exceed the profit it is drawn from, though this dictionary does not enforce that cross-form ceiling — see below). UNANSWERED POSTURE: refused/defaulted to $0 through /primaryFilerScheduleSeNotaryNetProfitAsCombined — the notary exclusion is not applied, which is the honest default (this dictionary cannot infer notary status from a Schedule C alone) rather than a guess that could either over- or under-exclude. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. No Max is enforced here; the printed instruction implies the entry cannot exceed the filer's total Schedule C net profit, but no template in this module can express a cross-fact ceiling as a Limit, so a filer-entered amount above their net profit is accepted and simply drives line 3 (and the EITC/ACTC earned-income twins) below what the notary business alone earned. FEEDS: /primaryFilerScheduleSeNotaryNetProfitAsCombined, which subtracts it (already negated) from Schedule SE line 3 (/primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss), and from the same-shaped subtraction in /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome and /selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax.
WHOSE SCHEDULE SE: the PRIMARY filer's, this module's unqualified-path convention. A secondary-filer twin is owed whenever the MFJ two-Schedules-SE gap closes. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE notary profit exclusion input, floored at zero
Fact.Description: Complete-only nonnegative reading of /writableScheduleSeNotaryPublicNetProfit. The writable declares a minimum of zero, but that declaration is not enforced on the dependent resolution path; a negative persisted answer must not become positive earnings when the notary exclusion computes zero minus the entered amount. Unanswered input remains Incomplete here, while the existing complete-safe combined fact still supplies zero.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 2 — net earnings from ministerial services excluded under an approved Form 4361
Fact.Description:
Section 1402(e)/Form 4361 is EARNINGS-scoped, not return-scoped: the exemption reaches only the filer's earnings FROM THE EXERCISE OF MINISTRY (or as a Christian Science practitioner or a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty), never a minister's other, non-ministerial self-employment earnings — a minister who also runs an unrelated Schedule C business still owes SE tax on that business. This screen asks the filer to separate the two.
QUESTION TEXT: "How much of your self-employment net profit was net earnings from the exercise of your ministry (or your service as a Christian Science practitioner or a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty) that are exempt from self-employment tax under your approved Form 4361?" HELP TEXT: "If the IRS approved your Form 4361, Application for Exemption From Self-Employment Tax for Use by Ministers, Members of Religious Orders, and Christian Science Practitioners, your net earnings from ministerial services are excluded from self-employment tax. This exclusion applies ONLY to your ministerial earnings — enter just that part of your net profit. Do not enter net profit from a separate, non-ministerial trade or business; that income is still subject to self-employment tax." ASKED-WHEN: after the filer's Schedule C/K-1 income is entered, and after /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeIsMinisterOrReligiousOrderMember and /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeHoldsApprovedForm4361 — ask it when that second Boolean is answered TRUE. Asking it of a filer who has just answered NO produces the contradicted return the exclusion arm now refuses to honour, and asking it wherever there is line 2 net profit asks a minister's question of a bare Schedule C. UNANSWERED POSTURE: $0 through /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined — no exclusion applied, the honest default, because the amount cannot be inferred and a complete-safe $0 keeps line 3 resolvable on every return that never sees this screen. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0. No Max is enforced here, for the same reason /writableScheduleSeNotaryPublicNetProfit has none: no template in this module can express a cross-fact ceiling against the filer's total net profit as a Limit. FEEDS: /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined, which subtracts it (already negated, the CRP/notary idiom) from Schedule SE line 3 (/primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss) — non-ministerial earnings on the same Schedule C/K-1 stay in line 3 and are taxed normally.
HOW THIS RELATES TO /writableScheduleSeMinisterForm4361OtherEarnings (Schedule SE PART I CHECKBOX A). That fact is READ, NOT DUPLICATED: checkbox A is the printed CONJUNCTION of "you filed Form 4361" AND "you had $400 or more of OTHER (non-ministerial) net earnings" — it is TRUE only for a 4361 holder who ALSO clears the $400 non-ministerial threshold, and stays FALSE for a 4361 holder with no other earnings, who still excludes 100% of net profit here. The two facts are INDEPENDENT INTAKES about the same filer, not one derived from the other, because checkbox A's own population (has $400+ of OTHER earnings) is not knowable from this fact's dollar amount without also knowing the filer's total net profit, and this fact's dollar amount is not knowable from checkbox A's bare boolean. A filer who answers this screen with a positive ministerial exclusion and also has $400+ of non-ministerial earnings should see checkbox A TRUE on the printed Schedule SE; that print wiring is not built here (checkbox A stays its own unmodelled intake) and is residue.
HOW THIS RELATES TO /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeHoldsApprovedForm4361: that Boolean switches off the section 1402(a)(8) housing and meals add-back for a Form 4361 holder, and it GUARDS this amount in one direction only — an amount entered on a return that answered that Boolean FALSE is not excluded, because the filer has denied the very exemption the amount is claimed under. A BLANK Form 4361 answer leaves this amount excluded exactly as before; the Boolean is a contradiction check here, not a precondition of the exclusion.
WHOSE SCHEDULE SE: the PRIMARY filer's, this module's unqualified-path convention. The spouse's twin is /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE primary ministerial earnings exclusion input, floored at zero
Fact.Description: Complete-only nonnegative reading of /writableScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings. The writable declares a minimum of zero, but that declaration is not enforced on the dependent resolution path; a negative persisted answer must not become positive self-employment earnings when the ministerial exclusion computes zero minus the entered amount.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 3 ministerial-earnings exclusion, negated, complete safe
Fact.Description:
The section 1402(e)/Form 4361 ministerial-earnings exclusion as line 3 combines it: $0 minus /writableScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings when that intake was answered, and $0 otherwise. The exact idiom /primaryFilerScheduleSeNotaryNetProfitAsCombined and /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bAsCombined already use, applied to the ministerial exclusion.
WHY IT IS NEGATED HERE RATHER THAN SUBTRACTED THERE, and WHY IT IS COMPLETE SAFE: identical reasoning to the notary twin — negating at this one place keeps /primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss a literal Add of the line-3 components, and a raw Dependency on the bare writable would make line 3 and everything downstream of it Incomplete on every return that does not answer the ministerial screen, which is nearly all of them.
WHAT IT DOES TO THE TAX. IRC 1402(e) excludes net earnings from the exercise of ministry (under an approved Form 4361) from "net earnings from self-employment" outright — narrower than the section 1402(g)/1401(c) exemptions modelled on /primaryFilerIsExemptFromSelfEmploymentTax, which zero a filer's ENTIRE chapter-2 liability; this exclusion removes only the ministerial PORTION of net profit from line 3, so a minister's non-ministerial Schedule C or K-1 earnings on the same return keep being taxed normally.
READ BY BOTH EARNED-INCOME RECONSTRUCTIONS, like the notary term, so each equals the actual Schedule SE line 3: /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome (EIC Worksheet B line 1a; Publication 596, "amounts you received for performing ministerial duties, but not as an employee, don't count as earned income" under an approved Form 4361) and /selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax (Schedule 8812 line 18a; the Earned Income Worksheet's "Do not include ... any other amounts exempt from self-employment tax").
WHOSE SCHEDULE SE: the PRIMARY filer's, matching this module's unqualified-path convention. The spouse's twin is /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Schedule SE line 3 — net earnings from ministerial services excluded under her approved Form 4361
Fact.Description: The spouse's twin of /writableScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings, for her own Schedule SE on a joint return. Section 1402(e) is granted to an individual and is earnings-scoped: her approved Form 4361 excludes her earnings from the exercise of ministry and nothing else. QUESTION TEXT: "How much of your spouse's self-employment net profit was net earnings from the exercise of ministry (or service as a Christian Science practitioner or a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty) that are exempt from self-employment tax under your spouse's approved Form 4361?" HELP TEXT: as the primary filer's screen; enter only the ministerial part of her net profit. ASKED-WHEN: the spouse has Schedule SE line 2 net profit of her own AND /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeHoldsApprovedForm4361 is answered TRUE (the primary twin's asked-when). UNANSWERED POSTURE: $0, no exclusion, through /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined (the primary twin's posture); entered on a return that answered her Form 4361 Boolean FALSE it is guarded out, also the primary twin's behaviour. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0; no cross-fact ceiling, for the primary twin's reason. FEEDS: /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined, subtracted from her line 3 (/secondaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss); the primary filer's chain never reads it. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE secondary ministerial earnings exclusion input, floored at zero
Fact.Description: Complete-only nonnegative reading of /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings. The writable declares a minimum of zero, but that declaration is not enforced on the dependent resolution path; a negative persisted answer must not become positive self-employment earnings when the spouse's ministerial exclusion computes zero minus the entered amount.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Schedule SE line 3 ministerial-earnings exclusion, negated, complete safe
Fact.Description: The spouse's twin of /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined: $0 minus /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings when answered, and $0 otherwise, so her line 3 stays a literal Add and stays Complete on every return that never sees her screen. Same complete-safe idiom as the notary and CRP terms, plus the primary twin's contradiction guard: an amount entered while /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeHoldsApprovedForm4361 is answered FALSE is not subtracted. Also read by /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome and /selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax, for the primary twin's reason. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Primary filer is a minister or member of a religious order (section 1402(a)(8) add-back gate)
Fact.Description: QUESTION TEXT: "In 2025, were you a duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed minister of a church, or a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty, performing ministerial services?" HELP TEXT: ministers pay self-employment tax on ministerial earnings even when paid as an employee, and the rental value of a home or a housing allowance and the value of meals and lodging furnished for the employer's convenience count toward those earnings although they are not taxed as income (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 1). A Christian Science practitioner answers no: section 1402(a)(8) names ministers and members of religious orders only. ASKED WHEN: the primary filer has earnings from a church or religious organization, or reports ministerial fees on Schedule C. UNANSWERED POSTURE: not a minister, the module's convention for a status the graph cannot infer; the add-back is $0 and every return that never sees the screen stays Complete. VALIDATION: Boolean. FEEDS: /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack, which asks the two amounts only when this is true. WHY A scheduleSE QUESTION RATHER THAN eitc:/writableIsClergyFilingScheduleSE: that fact is return-level and is the Form 1040 line 27b box, whose population is a clergy filer whose Schedule SE line 2 includes an amount also on Form 1040 line 1z; a minister whose line 2 is Schedule C fees plus a housing allowance is outside it, and a joint return needs the answer per spouse.

Fact.Name: Primary filer holds an approved Form 4361 exemption (section 1402(e))
Fact.Description: QUESTION TEXT: "Has the IRS approved your Form 4361, Application for Exemption From Self-Employment Tax for Use by Ministers, Members of Religious Orders, and Christian Science Practitioners?" HELP TEXT: an approved Form 4361 exempts your earnings from ministerial services from self-employment tax, and that includes a parsonage or housing allowance and meals and lodging furnished to you; your other self-employment earnings stay taxable (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 1). ASKED WHEN: /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeIsMinisterOrReligiousOrderMember is true. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED. A blank answer from a filer whose minister gate is already true is an unfinished interview, not a default, and BOTH defaults err: read as "no approved Form 4361" it applies the adverse add-back to a holder who skipped this screen, and read as "holds one" it drops the add-back for every minister who does not. The Form 4029 and totalization twins may default to "not exempt" because they sit behind no population gate, so a blank there means the filer never entered that territory; here the filer has already said "I am a minister" and this screen's own ASKED WHEN is that answer. So /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack resolves Incomplete, through line 3 and the self-employment tax, until this screen is answered either way. VALIDATION: Boolean. FEEDS: /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack, which is $0 when this is true, so the housing and meals of an exempt minister are never taxed on top of the ministerial earnings /writableScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings already excludes. It also guards that exclusion against its own contradiction: answered FALSE it blocks /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined from subtracting an amount the filer has just said no approved Form 4361 covers. Left blank it blocks nothing there, so every return that predates this Boolean keeps its exclusion.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's parsonage rental value or housing allowance, including utilities (Schedule SE line 2)
Fact.Description: QUESTION TEXT: "What was the rental value of the home furnished to you, or the housing allowance paid to you, for your ministerial services in 2025, including payments for utilities?" HELP TEXT: include the full rental value or allowance even though it is not taxable income; enter $0 if you received none. Do not include retirement benefits from a church plan (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 1). ASKED WHEN: /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeIsMinisterOrReligiousOrderMember is true and /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeHoldsApprovedForm4361 is answered NO (a YES makes the add-back $0 without these amounts; a BLANK refuses). UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED while the gate is true; the add-back resolves Incomplete through line 3 and the self-employment tax. A $0 default would be the under-collect this screen exists to stop. VALIDATION: Dollar, minimum $0. FEEDS: /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack, less the after-retirement part.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's parsonage or housing allowance provided after retirement (not added back)
Fact.Description: QUESTION TEXT: "How much of that rental value or housing allowance was provided after you retired?" HELP TEXT: a home or housing allowance provided after you retire is not included in self-employment earnings (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 1). Enter $0 if you had not retired. ASKED WHEN: /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingValue is answered with an amount above $0. UNANSWERED POSTURE: $0, nothing subtracted, the module's convention for a filer-favourable reduction (it over-collects for a retired minister who skips the screen). VALIDATION: Dollar, minimum $0; an entry above the housing amount is floored so it never reduces the meals and lodging amount. FEEDS: /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack, subtracted from the housing amount.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's section 119 meals and lodging furnished for the employer's convenience (Schedule SE line 2)
Fact.Description: QUESTION TEXT: "What was the value of meals and lodging provided to you, your spouse, and your dependents for your employer's convenience for your ministerial services in 2025?" HELP TEXT: include it even though it is not taxable income; enter $0 if none. Do not count a home already entered as a parsonage or housing allowance (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 1). ASKED WHEN: as /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingValue. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED while the gate is true, for the same reason as the housing amount. VALIDATION: Dollar, minimum $0. FEEDS: /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's after-retirement housing amount, complete safe
Fact.Description: /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAfterRetirement when answered, and $0 otherwise, so a minister who never reaches that screen keeps the add-back Complete with nothing subtracted. The subtrahend of /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's section 1402(a)(8) minister add-back on Schedule SE line 2
Fact.Description: The amount the primary filer's Schedule SE line 2 includes for a minister: the parsonage rental value or housing allowance less the part provided after retirement (floored at $0), plus the section 119 meals and lodging. $0 when the filer is not a minister or member of a religious order (or never answered), and $0 when the filer holds an approved Form 4361, whose exemption reaches the housing and meals with the rest of the ministerial earnings. INCOMPLETE, deliberately, in TWO cases: when the filer is a minister and the approved-Form-4361 question itself is unanswered, and when the filer is a minister who answered it NO and either amount is unanswered. The add-back is adverse to the filer, so a default of $0 would reproduce the under-collect; and a blank Form 4361 answer errs one way or the other whichever value it is defaulted to, so it is refused instead. Added to line 3 by /primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss, printed in line 2 by /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine2, and read by /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome for EIC Worksheet B; kept out of /selfEmploymentEarnedIncomeSubjectToUsTax, whose Schedule 8812 line 18a route subtracts it. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer is a minister or member of a religious order (section 1402(a)(8) add-back gate)
Fact.Description: The spouse's twin of /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeIsMinisterOrReligiousOrderMember, asked of the secondary filer on a joint return: "In 2025, was your spouse a duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed minister of a church, or a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty, performing ministerial services?" Same help text, unanswered posture (not a minister, $0) and validation. FEEDS: /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack on her own Schedule SE; the primary filer's chain never reads it.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer holds an approved Form 4361 exemption (section 1402(e))
Fact.Description: The spouse's twin of /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeHoldsApprovedForm4361: "Has the IRS approved your spouse's Form 4361?" ASKED WHEN: /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeIsMinisterOrReligiousOrderMember is true. Same help text, unanswered posture (REFUSED: her add-back resolves Incomplete until this is answered either way, for the primary twin's reason) and validation. FEEDS: /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack, which is $0 when this is true.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's parsonage rental value or housing allowance, including utilities (Schedule SE line 2)
Fact.Description: The spouse's twin of /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingValue, asked about her own ministerial services when /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeIsMinisterOrReligiousOrderMember is true and /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeHoldsApprovedForm4361 is answered NO. Same question, help text, unanswered posture (REFUSED while her gate is true) and validation (Dollar, minimum $0). FEEDS: /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's parsonage or housing allowance provided after retirement (not added back)
Fact.Description: The spouse's twin of /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAfterRetirement. Same question, help text, unanswered posture ($0, nothing subtracted) and validation (Dollar, minimum $0). ASKED WHEN: /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingValue is above $0. FEEDS: /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's section 119 meals and lodging furnished for the employer's convenience (Schedule SE line 2)
Fact.Description: The spouse's twin of /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterMealsAndLodgingValue, asked with her housing amount. Same question, help text, unanswered posture (REFUSED while her gate is true) and validation (Dollar, minimum $0). FEEDS: /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's after-retirement housing amount, complete safe
Fact.Description: The spouse's twin of /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAfterRetirementAsEntered: her answered amount, or $0 when unanswered. The subtrahend of /secondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's section 1402(a)(8) minister add-back on Schedule SE line 2
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterHousingAndMealsAddBack, on her own Schedule SE and measured against her own wage base and $400 threshold. Same three Cases and no catch-all: $0 when she is not a minister (or never answered), $0 with an approved Form 4361, housing less the after-retirement part (floored at $0) plus meals and lodging once her Form 4361 answer and both amounts are answered, Incomplete otherwise (her blank Form 4361 answer refuses, for the primary twin's reason). Added to her line 3 by /secondaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss and read by /selfEmploymentEarnedIncome. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This business is a section 475(a) securities/commodities DEALER, not a trader
Fact.Description: QUESTION TEXT: "Is this business a dealer in securities or commodities under section 475(a) — buying and selling to customers as inventory — rather than a trader trading for your own account?" ASKED WHEN: form8960:/writableSection475eTraderInFinancialInstrumentsOrCommoditiesElection is answered true and this Schedule C is claimed. HELP TEXT: the trader attestation you just answered describes a TRADER (section 475(e)(2)/1411(c)(2)(B)), whose trading gains and losses are capital-asset in character and excluded from self-employment income (section 1402(a)(3)). A DEALER under section 475(a) is different: dealing income is ordinary income from property "held primarily for sale to customers" — exactly the property section 1402(a)(3)(A)(ii) excludes from ITS exclusion — so a dealer's Schedule C profit or loss stays fully subject to self-employment tax. UNANSWERED POSTURE: this is a CONDITION OF ALLOWANCE, not a complete-safe intake — an unanswered dealer question on a return that has claimed the trader exclusion leaves that exclusion INCOMPLETE (see /primaryFilerScheduleSeTraderScheduleCExclusionAsCombined's Description); this dictionary never silently assumes "not a dealer". VALIDATION: Boolean. FEEDS the trader-carve-out gate below.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C's dealer-or-trader question has been answered
Fact.Description: Trivially complete safe: IsComplete never itself resolves Incomplete. One term of /scheduleSeAnyScheduleCDealerQuestionAnswered.

Fact.Name: This Schedule C is attested as a section 475(a) dealer business
Fact.Description: Complete safe false when unanswered — the same idiom form7206:/formW2s/*/form7206SCorporationW2Flagged uses for a per-item attestation flag. One term of /scheduleSeAnyScheduleCDealerAttested.

Fact.Description: Count of /scheduleCs/*/scheduleSeSection475aDealerQuestionAnswered > 0, guarded in the module's own collection shape (IsComplete and a nonempty /scheduleCs, else FALSE) so a return with no Schedule C reads false rather than propagating — the same guard form7206:/form7206ScheduleCPlanBusinessCount uses over the same collection. NAMED RESIDUE: this checks ANY Schedule C on the return, not specifically the one scheduleC:/scheduleCFiler attributes to the primary filer. Correct on every single-Schedule-C return, which is the whole population the trader attestation's own screen text ("is trading ... your ONLY trade or business") admits; a multi-Schedule-C return is already outside that population and is the same MFJ/two-Schedule-C residue /primaryFilerScheduleSeTraderScheduleCExclusionAsCombined already names.

Fact.Description: Count of /scheduleCs/*/scheduleSeSection475aDealerAttestedTrue > 0, same collection guard as /scheduleSeAnyScheduleCDealerQuestionAnswered. Complete safe false on every committed scenario today (no Schedule C answers the dealer question at all).

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule SE line 3: the line-2 dotted-line subtractions undone when line 2 is skipped
Fact.Description: When the primary filer elects the nonfarm optional method, Schedule SE line 2 is skipped and /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine2 is $0, so the Schedule C and K-1 earnings those dotted-line entries come out of never reach line 3. The notary public, Form 4361 ministerial and section 1402(a)(3) trader subtractions are all taken from line 2 earnings, so line 3 adds them back here, exactly offsetting them: without this term the subtraction would reduce line 3 below the skipped lines and lower line 4a. $0 when the method is not elected, so nothing moves on a return that does not skip line 2. The community income adjustment is not reversed: it belongs to line 3 itself, not to line 2.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Schedule SE line 3: the line-2 dotted-line subtractions undone when line 2 is skipped
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerScheduleSeNonfarmOptionalMethodDottedLineReversal. Her only line-2 dotted-line subtraction on this line 3 is the Form 4361 ministerial exclusion, so that is the one term added back when she elects the nonfarm optional method and skips line 2. $0 when the method is not elected.

Fact.Name: Refuse: a spouse the section 6013(g) or (h) election treats as a resident has self-employment income
Fact.Description: SCREEN TEXT (refusal): "You chose to treat a nonresident alien spouse as a U.S. resident, and that spouse has self-employment income. The election makes the spouse a resident for income tax only, not for self-employment tax, and this return cannot yet work out whether that spouse owes self-employment tax (it depends on residency during the year and on any international social security agreement). You can't file this return here." FIRES WHEN the Form 1040 nonresident alien spouse election is answered true (form1040 /writableForm1040NonresidentAlienSpouseElection) AND the spouse the election reaches (filers /writableSection6013ElectionNonresidentSpouse: the secondary filer when unanswered or answered so, the primary filer when answered so, either when both) has net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more, or church employee income, on his or her own Schedule SE (/primaryFilerIsSubjectToSelfEmploymentTax, /secondaryFilerIsSubjectToSelfEmploymentTax). WHY: the election treats the spouse as a resident only for chapter 1 and chapter 24, and section 1402(b) takes a nonresident alien's net earnings out of self-employment income unless a section 233 agreement covers the individual. This graph computes self-employment tax for every filer with $400 of net earnings, so without this refusal it charges chapter 2 tax the statute does not impose. Complete-safe FALSE on every return that does not make the election. NAMED RESIDUE: an electing spouse covered by a totalization agreement, or one resident for part of the year under section 6013(h), may owe the tax; both are refused rather than computed.

Fact.Name: Trader attestation on a joint return where the spouse has a Schedule C
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission on a joint return where the return-level trader attestation (form8960:/writableSection475eTraderInFinancialInstrumentsOrCommoditiesElection) is answered Yes and the secondary filer has a Schedule C net profit or loss other than zero (scheduleC:/secondaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit).
WHY IT REFUSES. The attestation is one question for the return: is trading in financial instruments or commodities "your ONLY trade or business". Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 3 section 1402(a)(3) trader exclusion, negated — a CLAIMING condition, not unconditionally complete safe
Fact.Description:
The section 1402(a)(3) trader carve-out as line 3 combines it: $0 minus the PRIMARY filer's own attributed Schedule C net profit or (loss) (scheduleC:/primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit) when the trader attestation (form8960:/writableSection475eTraderInFinancialInstrumentsOrCommoditiesElection) resolves true AND no Schedule C on the return is attested as a section 475(a) DEALER business (/scheduleSeAnyScheduleCDealerAttested false); $0 when the trader attestation is false or unanswered (unaffected, complete safe); and INCOMPLETE — never a silent $0 or a silent full exclusion — when the trader attestation is true but the dealer question (/scheduleCs/*/writableScheduleSeSection475aDealer) has not been answered on any Schedule C. The exact idiom /primaryFilerScheduleSeLine1bAsCombined, /primaryFilerScheduleSeNotaryNetProfitAsCombined and /primaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarningsAsCombined already use for the negation, applied to the trader exclusion (a named gap). THE TRADER ATTESTATION'S POPULATION IS NOT DEALER-FREE ON ITS OWN. The attestation's screen text asks TRADER STATUS (section 475(e)(2), via section 1411(c)(2)(B)) — a genuine trader's gains and losses are capital-asset in character and section 1402(a)(3) excludes them from self-employment income outright. A DEALER under section 475(a) is a DIFFERENT population: dealing income is ordinary income from property "held primarily for sale to customers" (section 1402(a)(3)(A)(ii)'s own exclusion is expressly for property that is NEITHER stock in trade NOR held primarily for sale to customers — a dealer's inventory is exactly the excluded-from-the-exclusion case), so a dealer genuinely OWES self-employment tax on ordinary dealing income and a truthful "yes" on the trader attestation says nothing about whether the filer is also, or instead, a dealer. Without the dealer question this fact would zero a dealer's Schedule C profit out of SE income on the strength of the trader attestation alone, a taxpayer-favourable error. The dealer discriminator (/scheduleCs/*/writableScheduleSeSection475aDealer) is a scheduleSE per-Schedule-C writable extending scheduleC's own /scheduleCs collection — the same cross-module-writable-on-another-module's-collection pattern form7206:/formW2s/*/writableForm7206IsSCorporationMoreThanTwoPercentShareholder already uses on /formW2s. A native home in scheduleC.xml (rather than this cross-module extension) is a possible future relocation.
WHY IT IS NEGATED HERE RATHER THAN SUBTRACTED THERE: identical reasoning to the CRP, notary and ministerial twins — negating at this one place keeps /primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss a literal Add of the line-3 components.
WHY IT IS *NOT* UNCONDITIONALLY COMPLETE SAFE ANY MORE, and why that is the correct direction rather than a regression: a bare-unguarded return-level attestation WOULD have to stay complete safe (the reasoning the CRP/notary/ministerial twins rely on: reading it as an unguarded Boolean would make line 3 Incomplete on every return that never answers it). But once the trader attestation IS true, this is no longer an unanswered-and-irrelevant question — it is an ANSWERED CLAIM OF A FAVOURABLE EXCLUSION, and the dealer question that decides whether that claim is honoured is a genuine CONDITION OF ALLOWANCE on it. The general rule this dictionary applies elsewhere (an unanswered condition of allowance on a CLAIMING return is Incomplete, never a silent favourable default) governs here: $0 is safe (and correct) when trader is false/unanswered, because nothing has been claimed; $0 is safe when dealer is affirmatively true, because the claim is affirmatively defeated; but defaulting a genuinely UNANSWERED dealer question to "not a dealer" would be exactly the silent favourable default the rule forbids, so this fact is deliberately Incomplete there instead. NO COMMITTED SCENARIO OR NODE FIXTURE PRE-DATING THIS FIX EVER ANSWERED THE TRADER ATTESTATION TRUE (verified before this fix: writable transcribed false on all 382 committed node fixtures that carry it, true on exactly the two form8960 fixtures this contract's own report names), so this new Incomplete branch is UNREACHABLE on every one of them — nothing that was Complete before this fix becomes Incomplete now.
WHY THE WHOLE SIGNED AMOUNT, NOT PROFIT ONLY, UNLIKE FORM 8960'S OWN TRADER FACTS: section 1402(a)(3) excludes the trader's Schedule C gain OR loss from self-employment income entirely (usc26-1402 lines 114-116, "there shall be excluded any gain or loss — which is considered as gain or loss from the sale or exchange of a capital asset"), not profit only. form8960:/niitSection475eTraderScheduleCProfit floors at profit because NIIT line 4a only ever adds income; this fact instead negates the attributed Schedule C term as entered, signed, so a trader's Schedule C LOSS is removed from net earnings from self-employment too, exactly as it is removed from NII by the sibling form8960:/niitSection475eTraderScheduleCNetLossModification's line-10 leg.
WHAT CHANGED IN THE TAX. Before this fact existed, a genuine section 475(e)(2) trader in financial instruments or commodities whose only business is that trading was taxed on Schedule SE on the same Schedule C profit form8960 correctly excludes from self-employment income for NIIT purposes — the same dollar taxed twice, once wrongly here and once rightly there. i8960 states the consequence in its own words: "If your only business is trading in financial instruments or commodities, you may use any net loss amount on your Schedule C ... as a deduction on line 10, and you don't need to complete Schedule SE (Form 1040)" (i8960:1469-1471). $0 on every committed node fixture and scenario: none answers the attestation true, so no committed return moves.
NAMED RESIDUE, carried verbatim from the contract because this unit does not resolve it: the attestation is RETURN-LEVEL, one question rather than one per spouse, so on an MFJ return where BOTH spouses separately own a Schedule C, a true attestation cannot by itself say which spouse's business is the trading business. This fact reads only the PRIMARY filer's OWN attributed Schedule C term, so it is wrong exactly when the trading business is attributed to the primary filer's Schedule C slot by default (scheduleC:/scheduleCFiler unanswered) while the trading business is actually the secondary filer's — a shape no committed scenario carries. The corpus's own two witnessed shapes (a single Schedule C attributed to the primary filer, and no Schedule C answered for either filer) are exactly the population section 1402(a)(3) and the attestation's own screen text describe. The dealer discriminator carries the SAME any-Schedule-C-on-the-return residue, named on /scheduleSeAnyScheduleCDealerQuestionAnswered's own Description.
WHOSE SCHEDULE SE: the PRIMARY filer's, matching this module's unqualified-path convention. A secondary-filer twin is owed whenever a committed scenario needs the trading business attributed to the secondary filer's own Schedule C. interpretation:provisional.

Enter 'Exempt community income' and the allocated amount. ... If the allocated amount is a net profit, subtract it from the total of lines 1a, 1b, and 2. If the allocated amount is a loss, treat it as a positive amount and add it." UNANSWERED POSTURE: complete safe $0. Fact.Name: The primary filer's wages as a U.S. citizen employed by a foreign government or an international organization
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "As a U.S. citizen, how much did you earn working for a foreign government, an international organization, or a wholly owned instrumentality of one?" HELP TEXT: enter the gross wages from that employment, and ONLY wages on which no U.S. social security or Medicare tax was withheld - if a Form W-2 was issued, boxes 4 and 6 must be empty. This is not ordinary employment: a foreign embassy, consulate or international organization withholds no FICA, so the law collects it as SELF-employment tax on Schedule SE line 2 instead - an inclusion, not a relief, and it applies whether or not a Form W-2 was issued. A WHOLLY OWNED INSTRUMENTALITY counts only IN CERTAIN CASES, the instructions' own phrase: section 3121(b)(12) reaches it only where the service is similar to service performed abroad by U.S. Government employees AND the Secretary of State has certified that the foreign government grants an equivalent exemption. Without that certification the service is ordinary employment, FICA is withheld, and nothing is entered here. ASKED WHEN: the primary answered that he worked for a foreign government or an international organization during the year; never shown otherwise. UNANSWERED POSTURE: BLANK ON THE RETURN and complete-safe $0 - a filer who was never asked has no such income and nothing is added. VALIDATION: Dollar, minimum $0, gross wages. WHAT IT FEEDS: Schedule SE line 2 on his own Schedule SE, but ONLY once the companion "where were the services performed" question is answered - see /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeForeignGovernmentServicesPerformedInUs.

Fact.Name: The primary filer performed that foreign-government service in the United States or a U.S. possession
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Were those services performed in the United States, Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands, or the U.S. Virgin Islands?" HELP TEXT: the place the work was DONE is what decides this, not where the employer is based and not where the pay came from. Work done in any of those places is subject to self-employment tax; the same work done anywhere else is exempt from it. ONE CARVE-BACK, in the statute rather than in the instructions: an individual TRANSFERRED to an international organization from a Federal agency under 5 U.S.C. 3582, who keeps a reemployment right, stays in ordinary FICA employment under section 3121(y) and does not belong on Schedule SE at all - such a filer enters no wages here. ASKED WHEN: the primary entered an amount in /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeForeignGovernmentEmployeeWages. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED - the return cannot be finished, because /primaryFilerScheduleSeForeignGovernmentEmployeeIncomeIncluded resolves Incomplete and carries that through line 3, the self-employment tax and AGI. It is not defaulted either way: defaulting YES would tax earnings the instructions call exempt, defaulting NO would drop earnings the instructions say must be reported on line 2. VALIDATION: Boolean, yes or no. WHAT IT FEEDS: whether the wages entered beside it reach Schedule SE line 2 at all. NOT ASKED HERE, and deliberately: the dual-citizen exception. A U.S. citizen who is ALSO a citizen of a country with a bilateral social security agreement may have that country's government work exempted, and this dictionary already models that relief once, on /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeExemptUnderTotalizationAgreement, which zeroes this filer's whole line 6. A second exemption path here would be a parallel one.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's foreign-government employee wages as Schedule SE line 2 includes them
Fact.Description:
The PRIMARY filer's foreign-government or international-organization wages as the printed line 2 takes them: the amount entered when the services were performed in the United States or one of the listed possessions, and $0 when they were performed elsewhere - the instructions' own two halves, "Report income from this employment on Schedule SE, line 2" and "If you performed services elsewhere ... those earnings are exempt from SE tax". AN INCLUSION, NOT A RELIEF, which is why it is added rather than subtracted: employment by a foreign government is outside the wage base that ordinary employment sits in, so section 1402(c)(2)(C) leaves the service inside "trade or business" and the tax is collected on Schedule SE. COMPLETE-SAFE $0 on every return that enters nothing, which is every committed scenario. INCOMPLETE, deliberately, when wages are entered and the geographic question is unanswered: the condition that decides whether the amount is taxed at all is unanswered on a return that reported the amount, and the refusal is the honest result rather than either default. WHERE THESE WAGES ENTER FOR INCOME TAX: income:/primaryFilerForeignGovernmentWagesOnLine1h puts the included amount on Form 1040 line 1h when no Form W-2 reported it, and income:/knockoutForeignGovernmentWagesEnteredWithFica refuses a FICA-withheld Form W-2 entered on both screens.
THE DUAL-CITIZEN EXCEPTION IS NOT RE-IMPLEMENTED HERE. It reaches the same filer through /primaryFilerIsExemptUnderTotalizationAgreement, which zeroes this filer's line 6 in full and therefore this term with it. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's fees as a fee-basis state or local government official
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "How much did you receive in fees as a state or local government official paid only on a fee basis?" HELP TEXT: a state, county, city or other local government office paid ONLY by fees (for example, fees charged for each filing, recording or ceremony) and not by a salary. Enter the fees for the year. Do not include fees you already reported on a Schedule C: those already reach Schedule SE line 2 through Schedule C line 31. Fact.Name: The primary filer's fee-basis position was paid solely by fees and not covered by a federal-state social security agreement
Fact.Description: SCREEN: "Was that position paid ONLY by fees, and NOT covered by a federal-state social security coverage agreement (a section 218 agreement)?" HELP TEXT: answer Yes only when both are true. If the position also paid a salary, or your state brought the position under social security by agreement, social security and Medicare tax is handled through your employer and self-employment tax does not apply to the fees; answer No. Your government employer can tell you whether the position is covered. ASKED WHEN: an amount was entered in /writablePrimaryFilerScheduleSeFeeBasisOfficialFees. UNANSWERED POSTURE: REFUSED - the fees entered cannot be placed, so /primaryFilerScheduleSeFeeBasisOfficialFeesIncluded resolves Incomplete and carries that through line 3 and the self-employment tax. It is not defaulted either way: Yes would tax fees the statute may exclude, No would drop fees the instructions include. VALIDATION: Boolean. WHAT IT FEEDS: whether the fees entered beside it reach Schedule SE line 2.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's fee-basis official fees as Schedule SE line 2 includes them

Fact.Name: Primary filer's self-employment income is exempt under a totalization agreement (section 1401(c))
Fact.Description: PRIMARY FILER'S half of Schedule 2 line 4 box 3, the "Other" box, read here for the ONE "other" exemption this dictionary models: the section 1401(c) relief from SE tax for self-employment income that a bilateral Social Security "totalization" agreement between the US and a foreign country subjects EXCLUSIVELY to that foreign country's own system. QUESTION TEXT: "Is your self-employment income exempt from U.S. self-employment tax under a Social Security totalization agreement between the United States and another country?" HELP TEXT: "A totalization agreement can exempt your self-employment income from U.S. Social Security and Medicare taxes if it is instead subject exclusively to the other country's social security system. This applies only to YOUR OWN self-employment income, not your spouse's (IRC section 1401(c))." ASKED-WHEN: whenever this filer has any Schedule SE line 3 net profit. UNANSWERED POSTURE: defaulted to FALSE via /primaryFilerIsExemptUnderTotalizationAgreement's IsComplete/Switch guard. VALIDATION: Boolean. FEEDS: /primaryFilerIsExemptUnderTotalizationAgreement and, through it, /primaryFilerIsExemptFromSelfEmploymentTax — the same zeroing arm the Form 4029 twin feeds (line 6, SE tax, the section 164(f) deduction, and this filer's share of scheduleSE:/netEarningsFromSelfEmployment). Also feeds the return-level print box at /scheduleSeExemptFromSelfEmploymentTaxOther, which is now Any(this filer's twin, the secondary filer's twin); the free-text companion /writableScheduleSeExemptFromSelfEmploymentTaxOtherDescription STAYS RETURN-LEVEL (not twinned) — the printed form asks for one description regardless of which filer, or both, claims a box-3 exemption. "Other" is broader than totalization on the printed form (any exemption besides Form 4361 and Form 4029), but totalization is the only box-3 population this dictionary can identify a statutory basis for and zero; a filer who checks box 3 for a DIFFERENT reason still sees the box print TRUE (through the untouched free-text/attestation path this fact does not model) but this pass's zeroing does not fire for them. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Primary filer is exempt from self-employment tax under section 1402(g) or 1401(c)
Fact.Description: TRUE when the PRIMARY filer holds EITHER the Form 4029 exemption (/primaryFilerIsExemptUnderSection4029) or the totalization-agreement exemption (/primaryFilerIsExemptUnderTotalizationAgreement) — both exempt "the self-employment income of an individual" from the whole of chapter 2 (SE tax under section 1401 in full, including the Additional Medicare Tax on self-employment income Form 8959 computes from it), not merely the section 1401 SE-tax line item, so one Any() gates every consumer either exemption zeros. THE ZEROING ARM: /primaryFilerTotalNetEarningsSubjectToSeTax (Schedule SE line 6) is $0 when this is TRUE, which cascades to $0 on this filer's line 10 (social security portion), line 11 (medicare portion), line 12 (SE tax, /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentTax), line 13 (the section 164(f) deduction, /primaryFilerSelfEmploymentTaxDeduction — 50% of a zero line 12 is zero), and this filer's share of scheduleSE:/netEarningsFromSelfEmployment, which form8959:/additionalMedicareTaxOnSelfEmployment reads directly and independently of Schedule SE's own tax lines. NOT A KNOCKOUT: line 3 (/primaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss) and everything upstream of it (Schedule C net profit, AGI, QBI, EITC/ACTC earned income) are UNCHANGED — the exemption reaches chapter 2 only, not income tax, and this filer's return still files a Schedule SE showing the exempt earnings with a $0 tax, exactly as i1040sse describes for an exempt filer. PER-FILER, NOT RETURN-LEVEL: this fact governs the primary filer's OWN Schedule SE only; /secondaryFilerIsExemptFromSelfEmploymentTax is the independent twin, so an MFJ return where only one spouse holds an exemption zeros only that spouse's chain. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer is exempt from self-employment tax under section 1402(g) or 1401(c)
Fact.Description: The secondary filer's twin of /primaryFilerIsExemptFromSelfEmploymentTax: TRUE when the SECONDARY filer holds either exemption on her own Schedule SE. Zeros /secondaryFilerTotalNetEarningsSubjectToSeTax (line 6) and everything that fact feeds on the secondary chain (lines 10-13, and her share of scheduleSE:/netEarningsFromSelfEmployment), leaving the primary filer's chain and both filers' line-3 net profit (income tax base) unchanged. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Schedule 2 line 4 box 1: an approved Form 4361 exemption from the self-employment tax (filer entry)
Fact.Description: The first exemption box printed on Schedule 2 line 4, "Check if any exemption from (see instructions): 1 4361". TRUE when the filer holds an approved Form 4361 exemption. A DIFFERENT ATTESTATION FROM /writableScheduleSeMinisterForm4361OtherEarnings, which this module already carries: that one is Schedule SE Part I checkbox A and is the CONJUNCTION of an approved Form 4361 and $400 or more of OTHER net earnings from self-employment, so it is false for a Form 4361 holder with no other earnings, who still checks this Schedule 2 box. This fact is the bare exemption, and the obligation asks that Schedule SE checkbox A be re-derived from it rather than asking the Form 4361 question twice. Print only; nothing computed changes, exactly as the Schedule SE checkbox records for itself. UNLIKE THE 4029/TOTALIZATION BOXES ABOVE, this box is NOT rebuilt per-filer: section 1402(e) is EARNINGS-scoped, not return-scoped (a 4361 minister's NON-ministerial earnings stay taxed), so its exclusion is modelled as a per-filer dollar amount at /writableScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings and /writableSecondaryFilerScheduleSeMinisterialNetEarnings, not as a boolean zeroing arm on this box. NOT RE-DERIVED from the per-filer facts either, unlike the 4029 box: the instructions give this box a second conjunct ("If you had no other income subject to SE tax, check box number 1 for Form 4361 on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 4", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sse.pdf, page 1, RIGHT column), so it is not Any() of the per-filer /writable{Primary,Secondary}FilerScheduleSeHoldsApprovedForm4361 answers. This box stays a bare, unmodelled attestation.
